karl-rove.summary: Indonesian general; former Chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff of Indonesia; banned from the United States on human-rights grounds for personally killing six pro-democracy college student protesters by stabbing each in the heart in front of the others; subsequently elected Vice President of Indonesia; subject of an unsuccessful 2008 reputation-rehabilitation campaign conducted by John Rendon's firm with Karl Rove and John Kiriakou.

karl-rove.title: John Rendon
karl-rove.summary: Self-described "professional propagandist"; organizer of the pre-distributed American flags waved by Kuwaiti crowds on the 1991 Kuwait Liberation Day; in 2008 hired John Kiriakou (alongside Karl Rove) to produce op-eds attempting to rehabilitate the U.S. travel ban imposed on Indonesian general Joko Widodo.

karl-rove.title: John Kiriakou
karl-rove.summary: American former CIA counterterrorism officer, whistleblower, author, and podcast host

karl-rove.title: Kuwait Liberation Day
karl-rove.summary: February 1991 expulsion of Iraqi forces from Kuwait by the U.S.-led coalition; John Kiriakou entered the country with U.S. Marines on the day of liberation; the small American flags waved by the crowds — and the post-liberation arrival of Democratic and Republican National Committee personnel ostensibly to assist the country's transition to democracy — were, per Kiriakou, the work of professional propagandist John Rendon.

karl-rove.title: National Endowment for Democracy
karl-rove.summary: U.S. federally chartered organization characterized by John Kiriakou as a proxy for CIA propaganda — the funding vehicle by which the agency promotes pro-U.S. political leaders in foreign countries; explicitly not an operational entity in the boots-on-the-ground sense.

kashmir.title: India
kashmir.summary: The country John Kiriakou names as his least favourite of all the places he has worked — not, he stresses, for poverty or danger, both of which he has seen worse of, but for the caste system and "the way Indians treat one another." His illustration is an afternoon in Hyderabad when two separate restaurants refused to admit the driver he had invited to lunch.

kashmir.title: Imran Khan
kashmir.summary: Former Prime Minister of Pakistan; subsequently deposed and imprisoned; his political party, the PTI (Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf), sent John Kiriakou a formal demand for apology after a November 2025 Indian-media interview in which Kiriakou observed that India would prevail over Pakistan in a conventional conflict; Kiriakou's reply has not been transcribed in polite company.

kashmir.title: Pakistan Station (2002)
kashmir.summary: John Kiriakou's January 2002 arrival in Islamabad to become CIA chief of counterterrorism operations — a journey via London and Kuwait with lost luggage, a warning that steered him away from the soon-to-be-bombed Marriott, a skeleton counterterrorism branch of seven CIA retirees, and the raids that followed.

kashmir.title: Advanced Counterterrorism Operations
kashmir.summary: The six-week specialist course at CIA headquarters that John Kiriakou attended roughly eighteen months before 9/11 as one of fourteen officers selected worldwide — weapons, explosives, counterterrorist and desert driving, bugs, cameras, satellites and drones — and which, by accident of timing, meant a cadre was trained and able to deploy the moment the attacks came.

kashmir.title: Spies of Arlington National Cemetery
kashmir.summary: On the Walk With History podcast, John Kiriakou — author of Remains of the Day: A Definitive Guide to Washington D.C.''s Historic Cemeteries — toured Arlington National Cemetery and told personal and historical stories about the intelligence figures buried there, including OSS founder William Donovan, deputy CIA director Vernon Walters, codebreakers William and Elizabeth Friedman, slain station chiefs Richard Welch and William Buckley, U-2 pilot Francis Gary Powers, and Mike Spann, the first CIA officer killed after 9/11.

kashmir.title: Bab al-Mandab
kashmir.summary: The strait where the Horn of Africa nearly meets the south-western tip of the Arabian Peninsula, which John Kiriakou identifies as one of the few American national interests in Yemen and as a chokepoint whose closure would push the global economy into recession.

kathryn-ruemmler.title: John Brennan
kathryn-ruemmler.summary: Former Director of the CIA; characterized in KiriPedia's source corpus as the principal architect of the agency's enhanced interrogation program and as having plotted against an elected President

kathryn-ruemmler.title: Jeffrey Epstein
kathryn-ruemmler.summary: Convicted sex offender; per John Kiriakou, was "an Israeli access agent" rather than a CIA asset, because the CIA collects foreign intelligence and Epstein's targets — Bill Clinton, Bill Gates, Prince Andrew — were not foreign. Kiriakou further holds that Epstein did die by suicide in federal custody, because in the Bureau of Prisons the cameras never work and the guards are always asleep.

kathryn-ruemmler.title: Tuesday morning kill list
kathryn-ruemmler.summary: Weekly CIA targeting meeting instituted by John Brennan in 2009 during his service as Deputy National Security Advisor for Counterterrorism in the Obama administration; produced a written list of individuals to be killed in the following week; per John Kiriakou, the program was a source of pride within the Obama administration and was made operationally possible by the targeting-software sophistication of the period.

kathryn-ruemmler.title: FCI Loretto
kathryn-ruemmler.summary: U.S. Federal Correctional Institution in Loretto, Pennsylvania; the low-medium-security prison at which John Kiriakou served 23 months of a 30-month sentence following his 2013 Espionage Act–era plea deal; the originally ordered "minimum security work camp" placement was countermanded — per Kiriakou, on Brennan's direct intervention — to place him in the actual prison alongside the general population.

kathryn-ruemmler.title: 2026 Iran war
kathryn-ruemmler.summary: The open-ended American and Israeli war against Iran that John Kiriakou tracked week by week on his own show — a conflict he says was sold as three weeks, ran into its fifth month, achieved every decapitation objective it set, and continued anyway. His grade for it is a D, and his forecast is a Truth Social post declaring victory while nothing changes.

kathryn-ruemmler.title: James Clapper
kathryn-ruemmler.summary: Director of National Intelligence under Obama; John Kiriakou recounts Clapper being pressed by Senator Rand Paul on whether the president could legally use a drone to kill an American on U.S. soil who had never been charged — the eventual answer being yes.

ken-dilanian.title: Jason Leopold
ken-dilanian.summary: Bloomberg investigative journalist; characterized by John Kiriakou as the leading practitioner of Freedom of Information Act litigation against U.S. [intelligence agencies](/wiki/intelligence-agencies); broke the Hillary Clinton private-email-server story; whose FOIA suit against the CIA Office of Public Affairs produced documentary evidence that NBC's chief national-security correspondent had been sending articles to the CIA for clearance before sending them to his own editor.

ken-dilanian.title: Central Intelligence Agency
ken-dilanian.summary: U.S. foreign intelligence service; John Kiriakou's employer from 1990 to 2004 and the central institution of KiriPedia

ken-dilanian.title: John Kiriakou
ken-dilanian.summary: American former CIA counterterrorism officer, whistleblower, author, and podcast host

ken-dilanian.title: Operation Mockingbird
ken-dilanian.summary: The CIA's mid-twentieth-century program of recruiting and managing American journalists as influence assets; in John Kiriakou's account, no longer operationally necessary in the contemporary period because the U.S. media voluntarily reprints CIA-supplied material, and in at least one documented case sends articles to the agency for clearance before sending them to its own editor.

ken-dilanian.title: Abu Zubaydah
ken-dilanian.summary: Detainee captured by John Kiriakou's CIA team in Pakistan in March 2002; the first subject of the agency's enhanced interrogation techniques program; subjected to both approved and unauthorized techniques including the cockroach-in-coffin treatment exploiting a documented insect phobia.

ken-dilanian.title: Church Committee
ken-dilanian.summary: U.S. Senate investigative committee operating in 1975–1976 that examined domestic intelligence abuses by the CIA, FBI, and NSA; per John Kiriakou, the Church Committee — alongside the concurrent Pike Committee in the House — was the last genuine moment of legislative oversight over the intelligence community, born of a national consensus that government had gone dangerously off course. Its work led to the creation of the permanent Senate Select Committee on Intelligence, which Kiriakou says ceased to function as real oversight roughly seven years after its founding.

kent-state.title: RFK Assassination
kent-state.summary: Assassination of Robert F. Kennedy on June 5, 1968 in Los Angeles; per John Kiriakou, physically impossible to attribute to Sirhan Sirhan alone — Los Angeles County coroner Thomas Noguchi determined the fatal shot was fired from behind and below Kennedy's right ear at close range while Sirhan stood in front, the crime scene yielded more bullets than Sirhan's revolver could hold, and a hotel security guard named 'Caesar' was captured on video standing behind Kennedy at the moment of the shooting.

kent-state.title: John Kiriakou
kent-state.summary: American former CIA counterterrorism officer, whistleblower, author, and podcast host

kent-state.title: JFK assassination
kent-state.summary: November 22, 1963 killing of President John F. Kennedy in Dallas, Texas. John Kiriakou's position, drawn from a Pakistan-station encounter with Bay of Pigs commander Jean Gately, an RFK Jr. account of CIA Director John McCone's same-day exchange with Bobby Kennedy Sr., and a White House contact's confirmation that the remaining classified Kennedy documents all contain the word "Israel," is that elements of the CIA were probably involved and that Israeli intelligence was involved as well.

kent-state.title: MK-Ultra
kent-state.summary: The CIA's mid-twentieth-century umbrella program of mind-control, behavioral-modification, and biological-warfare experimentation, encompassing subprojects such as MK-Chickwit and MK-Seesaw; active 1952–1975; documented practices included LSD dosing of unwitting American citizens in CIA-rented brothels and the aerosolized release of pathogens into the San Francisco fog; 80% of the program's documentation was destroyed by the CIA in defiance of a 1975 preservation order from Senator Frank Church.

kent-state.title: Al-Qaeda training manual interrogation-resistance tactics
kent-state.summary: A captured al-Qaeda training manual instructing operatives on how to resist interrogation, including feigning illness — a technique John Kiriakou says he saw a detainee use, and recognized, during a capture and interrogation in Pakistan.

kent-state.title: Asset acquisition cycle
kent-state.summary: The four-step process — spot, assess, develop, recruit — taught as the first lesson of CIA case officer training

khaled-mashal.title: Mahmoud al-Mabhouh
khaled-mashal.summary: Senior Hamas figure assassinated by Mossad in a Dubai hotel room in January 2010; the operation has been studied by intelligence services worldwide for its tradecraft, in particular the unsolved question of how the assassination team locked the hotel-room door from the inside after killing him.

khaled-mashal.title: MOSSAD
khaled-mashal.summary: Israel's primary external intelligence service; characterized by John Kiriakou as universally hostile in his and his CIA colleagues' professional dealings with it ("never had a positive encounter with Mossad"); operates almost exclusively in the operational rather than analytical domain; the CIA is, per Kiriakou, categorically forbidden from spying on it.

khaled-mashal.title: Access Agent
khaled-mashal.summary: CIA (and foreign intelligence service) term for a recruited asset whose value lies not in the secrets they hold directly but in their regular social access to high-value targets — politicians, executives, heads of state — who cannot themselves be recruited. Per John Kiriakou, the access agent is funded generously to maintain an environment in which the targets feel comfortable and return repeatedly; kompromat — compromising photographs or recordings — may be collected as a secondary tool. Kiriakou identifies Jeffrey Epstein as a textbook access agent, in his assessment working for Israeli intelligence.

khaled-mashal.title: AIPAC
khaled-mashal.summary: The American Israel Public Affairs Committee — the U.S. political organization that, in John Kiriakou's framing, ought to be registered as a foreign-lobbying entity but is not, and that wields decisive electoral power against U.S. elected officials who express support for Palestinian human rights.

khaled-mashal.title: Black Cube
khaled-mashal.summary: Israeli [private intelligence firm](/wiki/private-intelligence) staffed by former Mossad personnel; reportedly used by attorney David Boies in the Jeffrey Epstein litigation; named by John Kiriakou as a representative of the no-compunction operating posture characteristic of Israeli private and public intelligence.

khaled-mashal.title: Camp David Final Talks
khaled-mashal.summary: Middle East peace negotiations held at Camp David in the final days of the Clinton administration. Per John Kiriakou — relaying an account from a senior NSC officer who was present — the talks came extraordinarily close to a comprehensive agreement: with President Clinton, Vice President Al Gore, Yasser Arafat, Mahmoud Abbas, and Israeli Foreign Minister Shimon Peres around an enormous Sharpie-marked map of Jerusalem, dividing the city block by block. When the division was complete, Gore said ''My God, we have peace'' — and Arafat replied ''I can never sell this to the Palestinian people'' and walked out.

khalid-el-masri.title: Maher Arar
khalid-el-masri.summary: Canadian-Syrian political-science professor at the University of Toronto; in 2002, returning from a family visit in Tunis, was seized by the FBI at JFK at CIA request, secretly rendered to Damascus, and tortured by Syrian intelligence for eight to nine months until they concluded he was the wrong man. The U.S. denied any involvement to the Canadian government until Arar's wife produced a credit-card receipt from his return flight. He sued the U.S. and lost on national-security grounds, then sued the Canadian government and won six million dollars. Per John Kiriakou, his case is the canonical illustration of the CIA rendition program rendering the wrong person.

khalid-el-masri.title: Mohamedou Ould Slahi
khalid-el-masri.summary: Mauritanian citizen, medical student in Germany at the time of his 2001 detention; held at Guantánamo Bay for fourteen years on the basis of one phone call from his cousin asking him to relay news of a family death to a second cousin who was in al-Qaeda; identified by John Kiriakou as one of the most morally significant figures of the post-9/11 period; subject of the film The Mauritanian; became a personal friend of Kiriakou's after both men were released.

khalid-el-masri.title: Edward Snowden
khalid-el-masri.summary: Former NSA contractor who in 2013 disclosed the scope of U.S. [mass surveillance](/wiki/mass-surveillance), including the Section 702 collection program. Per John Kiriakou — who counts Snowden among the small group of national-security whistleblowers prosecuted under the Espionage Act — Snowden was ''stuck between two awful slippery slopes'': breaking his oath and chain of command on one side, and on the other catching something ''cut and dry against the Constitution'' that no one would act on. Kiriakou notes Snowden could not use his chain of command (as Kiriakou could not, his own chain being Jose Rodriguez), and that Judge Leonie Brinkema had reserved the Snowden case for herself before he fled the country.

khalid-el-masri.title: Enhanced interrogation techniques
khalid-el-masri.summary: The CIA's post-9/11 interrogation program; described by John Kiriakou as torture and as a euphemism designed to insulate the responsible officials from legal exposure.

khalid-el-masri.title: CIA Torture Program Whistleblowing
khalid-el-masri.summary: In December 2007, John Kiriakou became the first former CIA officer to publicly confirm the agency's post-9/11 torture program, telling ABC's Brian Ross that torture — including waterboarding — was official U.S. government policy personally approved by the president. Per Kiriakou, the decision followed a slow, incremental disillusionment dating back to a hooding incident in the field, years of waiting for someone else to come forward first, and culminated in prosecution under the Espionage Act after the program's congressional overseers publicly denied knowledge of what they had authorized and funded.

khalid-el-masri.title: Extraordinary Rendition
khalid-el-masri.summary: Per John Kiriakou, the CIA practice of seizing terrorism suspects in one country and transporting them to a third country — often a country with no due-process protections — to be held, interrogated, or tortured outside U.S. legal jurisdiction. The program operated alongside the enhanced-interrogation program and was the operational mechanism by which prisoners reached secret CIA facilities and allied torture sites in countries like Bahrain. Kiriakou himself was not in the rendition line of work but became a federal felon under the Intelligence Identities Protection Act for a single confirmation of a colleague's surname to a journalist who claimed to be writing a book on the Abu Omar rendition from Milan.

khalid-sheikh-mohammed.title: Abu Zubaydah
khalid-sheikh-mohammed.summary: Detainee captured by John Kiriakou's CIA team in Pakistan in March 2002; the first subject of the agency's enhanced interrogation techniques program; subjected to both approved and unauthorized techniques including the cockroach-in-coffin treatment exploiting a documented insect phobia.

khalid-sheikh-mohammed.title: Enhanced interrogation techniques
khalid-sheikh-mohammed.summary: The CIA's post-9/11 interrogation program; described by John Kiriakou as torture and as a euphemism designed to insulate the responsible officials from legal exposure.

khalid-sheikh-mohammed.title: Mitchell and Jessen
khalid-sheikh-mohammed.summary: The two American psychologists who pitched the CIA's enhanced interrogation program to Director George Tenet at a cocktail party in late October 2001; designers of the program and its theoretical underpinning, "learned helplessness."

khalid-sheikh-mohammed.title: CIA Torture Program Whistleblowing
khalid-sheikh-mohammed.summary: In December 2007, John Kiriakou became the first former CIA officer to publicly confirm the agency's post-9/11 torture program, telling ABC's Brian Ross that torture — including waterboarding — was official U.S. government policy personally approved by the president. Per Kiriakou, the decision followed a slow, incremental disillusionment dating back to a hooding incident in the field, years of waiting for someone else to come forward first, and culminated in prosecution under the Espionage Act after the program's congressional overseers publicly denied knowledge of what they had authorized and funded.

khalid-sheikh-mohammed.title: John Kiriakou
khalid-sheikh-mohammed.summary: American former CIA counterterrorism officer, whistleblower, author, and podcast host

khobar-towers-bombing.title: Hezbollah
khobar-towers-bombing.summary: Lebanese Shia militant organization and political party. Per John Kiriakou, Israel''s strategic goal regarding Hezbollah is not to defeat it outright but to keep Lebanon in a state of chaos that serves Israeli interests. He cites two Israeli operations: the simultaneous pager-detonation attack that decapitated Hezbollah''s leadership, which he called ''the most incredible operation I''ve ever seen,'' and the strike that killed former leader Hassan Nasrallah by leveling an entire complex and killing roughly 300 people — which he characterized as a war crime.

khobar-towers-bombing.title: Ali Soufan
khobar-towers-bombing.summary: FBI special agent who handled Abu Zubaydah immediately after his March 2002 capture; through patient, respectful interrogation produced the only actionable intelligence ever obtained from the detainee, including the first identification of "Mukhtar" as Khalid Sheikh Mohammed.

khobar-towers-bombing.title: CIA–FBI interagency rivalry and 9/11
khobar-towers-bombing.summary: John Kiriakou's account of the historical CIA–FBI rivalry, dating to J. Edgar Hoover's opposition to the 1947 National Security Act, and how it manifested before September 11 when Cofer Black's Counterterrorism Center withheld from the FBI that hijackers Nawaf al-Hazmi and Khalid al-Mihdhar had been granted U.S. visas.

khobar-towers-bombing.title: Counterterrorism Center
khobar-towers-bombing.summary: The CIA's Counterterrorism Center (CTC) — the unit where John Kiriakou spent the defining years of his operational career. He joined in the late 1990s as the only officer in the entire CIA fluent in both Greek and Arabic, served as chief of counterintelligence in the bin Laden unit, watched the Center swell from a few hundred employees to nearly 2,000 by September 12, 2001, and it was to CTC that he walked back down in May 2002 to refuse the torture program — the moment, he says, the CIA began to turn on him.

khobar-towers-bombing.title: John O'Neill
khobar-towers-bombing.summary: Special Agent in Charge of the FBI's New York field office for counterterrorism; "brash, flawed" but, per John Kiriakou, "spot-on about Osama bin Laden — 100 percent correct." Mentored FBI Arabic translator Ali Soufan. The principal subject of Lawrence Wright's book The Looming Tower.

khobar-towers-bombing.title: Kiriakou's transfer to the Directorate of Operations
khobar-towers-bombing.summary: John Kiriakou's roughly two-month internal campaign to transfer from the CIA's analytic Directorate of Intelligence to the operational Directorate of Operations, overcoming what he calls a "natural bias in operations against the eggheads on the analytic side," followed by an Athens posting secured because he was the only person in the entire CIA fluent in both Greek and Arabic. Covers his full CIA career arc from 1988/1990 recruitment through analyst years on Iraq, the switch to operations, 9/11, the enhanced-interrogation refusal, executive assistant to the deputy director for operations, and his eventual resignation and post-CIA career.

kiki-camarena-case.title: Overcriminalization
kiki-camarena-case.summary: John Kiriakou's argument that the United States criminalizes too much — locking up 25% of the world's prisoners with 5% of its population, and adding roughly 50 new felonies a year — illustrated by a NOAA employee prosecuted for whistling at a whale.

kiki-camarena-case.title: 9/11 Commission
kiki-camarena-case.summary: The federal commission of inquiry into the September 11 attacks, which John Kiriakou describes as structurally incapable of reaching the truth because it was barred from interviewing serving CIA officers or any Guantanamo detainee, and was blocked by the CIA from pursuing the Saudi thread.

kiki-camarena-case.title: Abu Zubaydah
kiki-camarena-case.summary: Detainee captured by John Kiriakou's CIA team in Pakistan in March 2002; the first subject of the agency's enhanced interrogation techniques program; subjected to both approved and unauthorized techniques including the cockroach-in-coffin treatment exploiting a documented insect phobia.

kiki-camarena-case.title: Afghan heroin policy
kiki-camarena-case.summary: The post-2001 U.S. policy in Afghanistan of protecting, and per John Kiriakou actively encouraging, the cultivation of heroin poppy. Under the Taliban in 2000 Afghanistan produced 0% of the world's heroin; by 2009 under American occupation it produced 93%. Per a DEA officer Kiriakou consulted with on the policy paper he was preparing for Senator Kerry, the strategic rationale was that nearly all of the heroin flowed to Iran and Russia, addiction in those countries was considered desirable as a long-run societal weakener, and the same logic now operates in reverse with Chinese fentanyl flowing into the United States.

kiki-camarena-case.title: Ahmed Khatib
kiki-camarena-case.summary: Iraqi-installed occupation governor of Kuwait announced on August 2, 1990, hours after the invasion; medical doctor trained at the American University of Beirut whose mother had been a Sudanese slave in the Kuwaiti royal household; college roommate of George Habash and co-founder of the Popular Front for the Liberation of Palestine.

kiki-camarena-case.title: Athens bank fraud report
kiki-camarena-case.summary: John Kiriakou's account of taking a dream job as COO of an Athens investment firm in 2020, discovering it was an elaborate bank fraud, and being unable to get the FBI to act — an agent telling him that without 'terrorism, China, or January 6th,' they were not interested.

kim-philby.title: James Jesus Angleton
kim-philby.summary: The CIA counterintelligence chief old-timers were 'genuinely afraid' of — and the wall of illegal files on American citizens kept in his office.

kim-philby.title: Operation Paperclip
kim-philby.summary: The program by which the CIA's predecessor brought Nazi scientists to the United States after World War II; John Kiriakou notes the FBI opposed it, that the Nazis surrendered to the U.S. fearing the Soviets, and that V-2 rocket father Wernher von Braun is buried near his home in Virginia.

kim-philby.title: Allen Dulles
kim-philby.summary: Long-serving CIA director whom John Kiriakou calls a 'monster' — a United Fruit board member who helped overthrow Guatemala's Arbenz, whose bust greeted visitors at CIA headquarters, and who was, unlike James Angleton, aware of his own guilt.

kim-philby.title: CIA sexpionage
kim-philby.summary: John Kiriakou''s account of the CIA''s use of sex in espionage — routine from its founding through the early 1980s, including MK-Ultra and honey-pot operations — and why the agency largely abandoned it: coercion cannot build the trust a long-term source requires. Other services never stopped.

kim-philby.title: Iran's 2024 drone retaliation
kim-philby.summary: John Kiriakou's account of Iran's telegraphed 2024 drone strike on Israel — hundreds of slow drones, launched with advance warning to the U.S. and Jordan, nearly all shot down, which he reads as a controlled show of force and an intelligence victory that exposed the Iron Dome.

kim-philby.title: Israel's cell-phone assassinations in Iran
kim-philby.summary: John Kiriakou's account of how Israel wiped out Iran's military leadership by tracking cell phones — recruiting destitute Afghan refugees as $100-a-month spotters, and, when the generals stopped carrying phones, targeting their bodyguards' phones instead.

king-abdullah-ii.title: Abraham Accords
king-abdullah-ii.summary: The Trump-brokered normalization deals between Israel and Gulf Arab states — in John Kiriakou's judgment "a terrible idea in the first place," a great victory for Israel and the Gulf Arabs that was "a punch in the throat to the Palestinians." He argues the Accords are how Trump meant to "solve the Middle East in a day" — by screwing the Palestinians — that Hamas read the abandonment correctly, that October 7 shattered the project, and that reviving the Accords (Saudis in, victory declared, Nobel collected) remains the organizing goal of Trump's regional policy.

king-abdullah-ii.title: Church of Saint Porphyrios
king-abdullah-ii.summary: The Greek Orthodox church in Gaza that John Kiriakou describes as the oldest continuously operating church in the world; per Kiriakou, Israel bombed it while 24 women and children were sheltering inside.

king-abdullah-ii.title: The 1991 Saudi plan for Gaza
king-abdullah-ii.summary: A proposal John Kiriakou says he watched Ambassador Chas Freeman float to the Saudis during his first overseas tour in 1991 — that Saudi Arabia fund a port, an airport, a desalination plant and an electrical grid in Gaza. The Saudis agreed; Israel refused outright. Kiriakou raises it because the identical arrangement resurfaced in the Israeli press more than three decades later.

king-abdullah-ii.title: Benjamin Netanyahu
king-abdullah-ii.summary: Israeli prime minister, per John Kiriakou an unpopular but politically durable figure whom Kiriakou says has spent decades pressing successive U.S. presidents to bomb Iran, presided over escalating land seizures in the West Bank, and used the October 7 attack and its aftermath to entrench his own political survival.

king-abdullah-ii.title: John Kiriakou
king-abdullah-ii.summary: American former CIA counterterrorism officer, whistleblower, author, and podcast host

king-abdullah-ii.title: Tucker Carlson
king-abdullah-ii.summary: American broadcaster and former Fox News host; a personal friend of John Kiriakou's for years, appearing on Kiriakou's radio and podcast work and hosting him roughly a dozen times on his own Fox show. Kiriakou calls him possibly the most brilliant and best-informed person he has ever encountered, and relays Glenn Greenwald's belief that Carlson could win the presidency — an idea Carlson privately dismisses.

kiriakou-and-cenk-uygur.title: AIPAC
kiriakou-and-cenk-uygur.summary: The American Israel Public Affairs Committee — the U.S. political organization that, in John Kiriakou's framing, ought to be registered as a foreign-lobbying entity but is not, and that wields decisive electoral power against U.S. elected officials who express support for Palestinian human rights.

kiriakou-and-cenk-uygur.title: Anwar al-Awlaki
kiriakou-and-cenk-uygur.summary: American-born al-Qaeda propagandist; in 1993 the imam of the Falls Church, Virginia mosque visited by John Kiriakou's CIA Arabic-language class on a field trip; in 2001 the cleric at whose mosque the 9/11 hijackers prayed the night before the attacks; killed by U.S. drone strike in Yemen in approximately 2011.

kiriakou-and-cenk-uygur.title: Benjamin Netanyahu
kiriakou-and-cenk-uygur.summary: Israeli prime minister, per John Kiriakou an unpopular but politically durable figure whom Kiriakou says has spent decades pressing successive U.S. presidents to bomb Iran, presided over escalating land seizures in the West Bank, and used the October 7 attack and its aftermath to entrench his own political survival.

kiriakou-and-cenk-uygur.title: Cofer Black
kiriakou-and-cenk-uygur.summary: Former head of the CIA Counterterrorism Center during and immediately after the September 11 attacks; principal architect of the agency's paramilitary turn on September 12, 2001; later Vice President of Blackwater under Erik Prince.

kiriakou-and-cenk-uygur.title: F-35 avionics dispute with Israel
kiriakou-and-cenk-uygur.summary: John Kiriakou's account of how Israel demanded F-35 fighters without the deliberately degraded avionics the U.S. installs on export models — and, refused, allegedly worked through American defense contractors to steal the technology instead.

kiriakou-and-cenk-uygur.title: Israeli integration into U.S. agencies
kiriakou-and-cenk-uygur.summary: John Kiriakou''s objection to the formal embedding of Israeli personnel inside American defense and intelligence institutions — a National Defense Authorization Act provision collocating them with the Pentagon and opening Five Eyes-style liaison with the CIA, arriving in the same weeks as a DIA all-hands warning that Israeli services were unusually aggressive in recruiting inside DIA. His argument is that the two cannot both be true: either Israel is a critical counterintelligence threat or it is a partner.

kiriakou-and-third-parties.title: Private prison system
kiriakou-and-third-parties.summary: John Kiriakou's account of the U.S. private prison industry as an incentive to keep beds filled and cut costs on food and medicine — illustrated by the 'sewer trout,' dog-food, and dead-rat-in-the-Kool-Aid stories from his own incarceration.

kiriakou-and-third-parties.title: Allen Dulles
kiriakou-and-third-parties.summary: Long-serving CIA director whom John Kiriakou calls a 'monster' — a United Fruit board member who helped overthrow Guatemala's Arbenz, whose bust greeted visitors at CIA headquarters, and who was, unlike James Angleton, aware of his own guilt.

kiriakou-and-third-parties.title: Arianna Huffington
kiriakou-and-third-parties.summary: Founder of the Huffington Post and the accidental amplifier who turned John Kiriakou's prison writing into a phenomenon. His first Letter from Loretto went to his attorney, then to a friend running Firedoglake who — unknown to Kiriakou — was close to Huffington; she plastered it as a banner headline and it drew over a million hits, bringing CNN and 60 Minutes to the prison gates. She published his open letter to Snowden, ran the diesel-therapy exposé that triggered the "hands off John Kiriakou" campaign, and came to Loretto herself with two young journalists.

kiriakou-cameo-practice.title: John Kiriakou
kiriakou-cameo-practice.summary: American former CIA counterterrorism officer, whistleblower, author, and podcast host

kiriakou-cameo-practice.title: 2026 Iran war
kiriakou-cameo-practice.summary: The open-ended American and Israeli war against Iran that John Kiriakou tracked week by week on his own show — a conflict he says was sold as three weeks, ran into its fifth month, achieved every decapitation objective it set, and continued anyway. His grade for it is a D, and his forecast is a Truth Social post declaring victory while nothing changes.

kiriakou-cameo-practice.title: Angry Birds
kiriakou-cameo-practice.summary: The mobile game John Kiriakou describes as his only vice besides buying art, played every morning for nine consecutive years and cited by his ex-wife as a grievance in their marriage.

kiriakou-cameo-practice.title: Benjamin Netanyahu
kiriakou-cameo-practice.summary: Israeli prime minister, per John Kiriakou an unpopular but politically durable figure whom Kiriakou says has spent decades pressing successive U.S. presidents to bomb Iran, presided over escalating land seizures in the West Bank, and used the October 7 attack and its aftermath to entrench his own political survival.

kiriakou-cameo-practice.title: Cameo
kiriakou-cameo-practice.summary: The personalised-video app John Kiriakou joined in February 2026 and turned into an unexpected second career — around 2,600 videos, roughly 900 of them in his first month alone. Half are birthday messages and most of the rest are requests for CIA stories, but about two hundred have been appeals for advice or a pep talk, and three of those people later told him he had talked them out of suicide.

kiriakou-cuba-trip.title: Gina Haspel
kiriakou-cuba-trip.summary: Director of the Central Intelligence Agency under President Trump's first term; known to John Kiriakou and others at the CIA as "Bloody Gina"; per Kiriakou, flew out to the secret black site to sit in on one of the enhanced-interrogation torture sessions "just because she could," personally supervised the torture of USS Cole bombing suspect Rahim al-Nashiri, and later fed the CIA's torture tapes into an industrial document grinder after being explicitly told by White House Counsel not to destroy them.

kiriakou-cuba-trip.title: Kiriakou's Russian media work
kiriakou-cuba-trip.summary: John Kiriakou's account of hosting a daily Sputnik radio show for seven and a half years with full contractual freedom to criticize anyone, including Putin — which he did on the morning of the Ukraine invasion — offered as a rebuttal to claims that Russian outlets are mere propaganda.

kiriakou-cuba-trip.title: Kiriakou's daily news diet
kiriakou-cuba-trip.summary: John Kiriakou's account of the wide range of mainstream and alternative outlets he reads each morning to compare competing angles, the two outlets — the Associated Press and ProPublica — he singles out as exceptional, and his broader habits of media consumption, from an admitted addiction to political polling to his distrust of AI chatbots after they repeatedly fabricated his own biography.

kiriakou-cuba-trip.title: Barack Obama
kiriakou-cuba-trip.summary: 44th U.S. president; in John Kiriakou's account, Obama publicly recounted refusing Benjamin Netanyahu's demand to bomb Iran and calling Israel's threat to use nuclear weapons a bluff — a bluff Kiriakou says Donald Trump later believed.

kiriakou-cuba-trip.title: Central Intelligence Agency
kiriakou-cuba-trip.summary: U.S. foreign intelligence service; John Kiriakou's employer from 1990 to 2004 and the central institution of KiriPedia

kiriakou-cuba-trip.title: Venezuelan embassy occupation (2019)
kiriakou-cuba-trip.summary: A 2019 sit-in at the Venezuelan embassy in Washington, D.C., which John Kiriakou says he joined at the Venezuelan government's request the night the United States broke relations with Venezuela; he says he still keeps Venezuelan government property from that night at his house.

kiriakou-cypriot-ancestry.title: The Green Line in Nicosia
kiriakou-cypriot-ancestry.summary: The division of Nicosia between the Republic of Cyprus and the Turkish-occupied north, which John Kiriakou toured in July 2026 and described as maintained through deliberate humiliation rather than any interest in settlement.

kiriakou-cypriot-ancestry.title: Origin of the Kiriakou name
kiriakou-cypriot-ancestry.summary: The Kiriakou surname originates in a clerical error at a Rhodes courthouse, where John Kiriakou's great-great-grandfather, arrested for stealing a potato while starving, gave a patronymic that was written down as his family name and never corrected.

kiriakou-cypriot-ancestry.title: Abu Zubaydah

kiriakou-cypriot-ancestry.title: Bureau of Prisons advisory board
kiriakou-cypriot-ancestry.summary: The advisory board John Kiriakou joined at the personal invitation of the Director of the Bureau of Prisons, who told him the president had tasked him with tearing the Bureau down and rebuilding it.

kiriakou-cypriot-ancestry.title: Edward Snowden
kiriakou-cypriot-ancestry.summary: Former NSA contractor who in 2013 disclosed the scope of U.S. [mass surveillance](/wiki/mass-surveillance), including the Section 702 collection program. Per John Kiriakou — who counts Snowden among the small group of national-security whistleblowers prosecuted under the Espionage Act — Snowden was ''stuck between two awful slippery slopes'': breaking his oath and chain of command on one side, and on the other catching something ''cut and dry against the Constitution'' that no one would act on. Kiriakou notes Snowden could not use his chain of command (as Kiriakou could not, his own chain being Jose Rodriguez), and that Judge Leonie Brinkema had reserved the Snowden case for herself before he fled the country.

kiriakou-daily-news-diet.title: Donald Trump
kiriakou-daily-news-diet.summary: 45th and 47th U.S. president. Per John Kiriakou, a man genuinely convinced he was doing right by bombing Iran, "duped" by the same Netanyahu nuclear bluff Obama once rejected — and, at the same time, the most blindly pro-Israel president in history, an admirer of autocrats who has never once criticized Vladimir Putin, and prone to gestures — from the Gulf of America to a since-abandoned "Department of War" rename — that test the edges of his actual authority.

kiriakou-daily-news-diet.title: Jeffrey Epstein
kiriakou-daily-news-diet.summary: Convicted sex offender; per John Kiriakou, was "an Israeli access agent" rather than a CIA asset, because the CIA collects foreign intelligence and Epstein's targets — Bill Clinton, Bill Gates, Prince Andrew — were not foreign. Kiriakou further holds that Epstein did die by suicide in federal custody, because in the Bureau of Prisons the cameras never work and the guards are always asleep.

kiriakou-daily-news-diet.title: Guantanamo Bay
kiriakou-daily-news-diet.summary: U.S. naval base in Cuba; site of CIA detention operations during the post-9/11 enhanced interrogation program; briefly served by John Kiriakou as interim Chief during the summer of 2002.

kiriakou-daily-news-diet.title: Saudi-Iran diplomatic rivalry
kiriakou-daily-news-diet.summary: John Kiriakou's account of the roots of Saudi-Iranian hostility — Iran's bloody 1979 infiltration of the Hajj, Saudi Arabia's suppression of its own Shia minority, and the 2023 restoration of diplomatic relations brokered, to Washington's surprise, by China.

kiriakou-death-threats.title: John Kiriakou's Briefing Room
kiriakou-death-threats.summary: A twice-weekly news and commentary programme launched by John Kiriakou in July 2026, presented as analysis rather than partisan opinion, and distinct from his storytelling podcast Dead Drop.

kiriakou-death-threats.title: Dead Drop (podcast)
kiriakou-death-threats.summary: John Kiriakou''s narrative podcast, launched in late 2025 — a season-long, memoir-style retelling of his life in intelligence, from recruitment ("The New Recruit") through Athens ("Golden Boy") to the post-9/11 hunt ("The Hunt Begins"), with mini-episodes like "A Spy''s Guide to Sofia." Written by Kiriakou with Alan Katz, produced by Costard & Touchstone Productions, with Kiriakou, Katz, and Nick Mechanic as executive producers. Its stated goal: "the deepest possible perspective on the world of spying and what makes any spy tick."

kiriakou-death-threats.title: Reza Pahlavi
kiriakou-death-threats.summary: The exiled Iranian crown prince whom John Kiriakou dismisses as an Israeli-backed fantasy candidate to rule Iran — a man who has not lived there since his teens, supported mainly by Beverly Hills exiles, whom Kiriakou says 'wouldn't survive the walk from the plane to the terminal.'

kiriakou-death-threats.title: Situational awareness
kiriakou-death-threats.summary: The discipline John Kiriakou describes as the civilian version of surveillance detection — get out of the kill zone at the first sign of trouble, keep an escape route, and refuse to let the brain rationalise away what it is seeing.

kiriakou-death-threats.title: John Kiriakou
kiriakou-death-threats.summary: American former CIA counterterrorism officer, whistleblower, author, and podcast host

kiriakou-death-threats.title: Kiriakou's television pilots
kiriakou-death-threats.summary: The eight television pilots John Kiriakou has sold over fifteen years as a hobby, beginning with Bomb Squad, a procedural about the New York City bomb squad built around a statistic that almost no bomb threat has anything to do with terrorism.

kiriakou-family-name.title: Kiriakou's Cypriot ancestry
kiriakou-family-name.summary: The DNA result showing John Kiriakou to be 24 per cent Cypriot — his largest single ancestry — which corrected a family belief that the line came from Crete and coincided with an invitation to address a Cypriot diaspora conference.
