sheldon-adelson.title: Israeli intelligence presence in the United States
sheldon-adelson.summary: John Kiriakou's account of Israeli intelligence activity inside the United States — dozens of undeclared Mossad and Shin Bet officers identified by the FBI, a critical-threat counterintelligence classification alongside Russia, North Korea and Cuba, and a pattern of harassment and intimidation directed at declared CIA officers posted to Israel.

sheldon-adelson.title: Donald Trump
sheldon-adelson.summary: 45th and 47th U.S. president. Per John Kiriakou, a man genuinely convinced he was doing right by bombing Iran, "duped" by the same Netanyahu nuclear bluff Obama once rejected — and, at the same time, the most blindly pro-Israel president in history, an admirer of autocrats who has never once criticized Vladimir Putin, and prone to gestures — from the Gulf of America to a since-abandoned "Department of War" rename — that test the edges of his actual authority.

sheldon-adelson.title: Edward Snowden
sheldon-adelson.summary: Former NSA contractor who in 2013 disclosed the scope of U.S. [mass surveillance](/wiki/mass-surveillance), including the Section 702 collection program. Per John Kiriakou — who counts Snowden among the small group of national-security whistleblowers prosecuted under the Espionage Act — Snowden was ''stuck between two awful slippery slopes'': breaking his oath and chain of command on one side, and on the other catching something ''cut and dry against the Constitution'' that no one would act on. Kiriakou notes Snowden could not use his chain of command (as Kiriakou could not, his own chain being Jose Rodriguez), and that Judge Leonie Brinkema had reserved the Snowden case for herself before he fled the country.

sheldon-adelson.title: Recruitment attempts on Kiriakou
sheldon-adelson.summary: A series of episodes in which foreign intelligence officers tried to recruit John Kiriakou himself — an over-eager Hungarian during his CIA application, a French counterterrorism officer who staged a car pickup in Islamabad, and a Shin Bet officer at his first liaison briefing.

shin-bet.title: Recruitment attempts on Kiriakou
shin-bet.summary: A series of episodes in which foreign intelligence officers tried to recruit John Kiriakou himself — an over-eager Hungarian during his CIA application, a French counterterrorism officer who staged a car pickup in Islamabad, and a Shin Bet officer at his first liaison briefing.

shin-bet.title: CIA adultery culture
shin-bet.summary: John Kiriakou's recurring characterization of the CIA officer corps as riddled with adultery and casual sex — which he frames not as gossip but as a systemic counterintelligence vulnerability that makes officers easy to recruit.

shin-bet.title: Donald Trump
shin-bet.summary: 45th and 47th U.S. president. Per John Kiriakou, a man genuinely convinced he was doing right by bombing Iran, "duped" by the same Netanyahu nuclear bluff Obama once rejected — and, at the same time, the most blindly pro-Israel president in history, an admirer of autocrats who has never once criticized Vladimir Putin, and prone to gestures — from the Gulf of America to a since-abandoned "Department of War" rename — that test the edges of his actual authority.

shin-bet.title: MOSSAD
shin-bet.summary: Israel's primary external intelligence service; characterized by John Kiriakou as universally hostile in his and his CIA colleagues' professional dealings with it ("never had a positive encounter with Mossad"); operates almost exclusively in the operational rather than analytical domain; the CIA is, per Kiriakou, categorically forbidden from spying on it.

shin-bet.title: Special Activities Division
shin-bet.summary: The CIA's paramilitary arm; described by John Kiriakou as having two organizationally distinct components — the pre-9/11 SAD, a covert-action division within the Directorate of Operations, and a post-9/11 special activities group within the Counterterrorism Center, staffed largely by personnel on secondment from Delta Force, SEAL Team 6, and other special-operations units.

shin-bet.title: Israeli intelligence presence in the United States
shin-bet.summary: John Kiriakou's account of Israeli intelligence activity inside the United States — dozens of undeclared Mossad and Shin Bet officers identified by the FBI, a critical-threat counterintelligence classification alongside Russia, North Korea and Cuba, and a pattern of harassment and intimidation directed at declared CIA officers posted to Israel.

shireen-abu-akleh.title: Church of Saint Porphyrios
shireen-abu-akleh.summary: The Greek Orthodox church in Gaza that John Kiriakou describes as the oldest continuously operating church in the world; per Kiriakou, Israel bombed it while 24 women and children were sheltering inside.

shireen-abu-akleh.title: Taybeh
shireen-abu-akleh.summary: The only fully Christian village in the West Bank, home to the Holy Land's oldest brewery; John Kiriakou recounts it being set on fire and its Marian festival attacked by the IDF with drones, helicopters and stun grenades.

shireen-abu-akleh.title: Roger Waters
shireen-abu-akleh.summary: Founding member of the British rock band Pink Floyd; outspoken supporter of Palestinian human rights; anonymously paid off John Kiriakou's second mortgage during his federal prison sentence, sparing his wife and children the loss of the family home; only discovered to be the benefactor years later; subsequently a personal friend of Kiriakou and a recurring guest on his programme.

shireen-abu-akleh.title: Benjamin Netanyahu
shireen-abu-akleh.summary: Israeli prime minister, per John Kiriakou an unpopular but politically durable figure whom Kiriakou says has spent decades pressing successive U.S. presidents to bomb Iran, presided over escalating land seizures in the West Bank, and used the October 7 attack and its aftermath to entrench his own political survival.

shireen-abu-akleh.title: Tuesday morning kill list
shireen-abu-akleh.summary: Weekly CIA targeting meeting instituted by John Brennan in 2009 during his service as Deputy National Security Advisor for Counterterrorism in the Obama administration; produced a written list of individuals to be killed in the following week; per John Kiriakou, the program was a source of pride within the Obama administration and was made operationally possible by the targeting-software sophistication of the period.

shireen-abu-akleh.title: Greek Intelligence Service
shireen-abu-akleh.summary: Greece's intelligence service, with which John Kiriakou worked closely during his Athens posting; its head of surveillance called off surveillance on him after watching him make a large offering at Saint Nectarios's tomb on the island of Aegina.

signature-strikes.title: CIA Torture Program Whistleblowing
signature-strikes.summary: In December 2007, John Kiriakou became the first former CIA officer to publicly confirm the agency's post-9/11 torture program, telling ABC's Brian Ross that torture — including waterboarding — was official U.S. government policy personally approved by the president. Per Kiriakou, the decision followed a slow, incremental disillusionment dating back to a hooding incident in the field, years of waiting for someone else to come forward first, and culminated in prosecution under the Espionage Act after the program's congressional overseers publicly denied knowledge of what they had authorized and funded.

signature-strikes.title: The Drone Papers
signature-strikes.summary: The trove of classified documents leaked by Daniel Hale and published by The Intercept — later collected in book form as 'The Assassination Complex' — exposing how the U.S. drone program selected and killed targets; John Kiriakou relied on it in his own writing on the war in Afghanistan.

signature-strikes.title: Anwar al-Awlaki
signature-strikes.summary: American-born al-Qaeda propagandist; in 1993 the imam of the Falls Church, Virginia mosque visited by John Kiriakou's CIA Arabic-language class on a field trip; in 2001 the cleric at whose mosque the 9/11 hijackers prayed the night before the attacks; killed by U.S. drone strike in Yemen in approximately 2011.

signature-strikes.title: PTSD
signature-strikes.summary: Post-traumatic stress disorder runs through John Kiriakou''s life and worldview — he had it coming out of Greece after an assassination attempt, brought it home from Pakistan alongside his shock at colleagues'' willingness to kill, and was blindsided by a delayed post-prison version that helped end his marriage. For six months after release he dreamed the same dream nightly: that he was out by mistake and had to get back inside before midnight count. He still takes a repurposed blood-pressure drug that stops the dreams, and he extends the diagnosis outward — to secret-site interrogators who came back crying, to drone pilots, and to prisoners released angry and untreated.

signature-strikes.title: Code Pink
signature-strikes.summary: The women-led peace group co-founded by Medea Benjamin. John Kiriakou first saw them as a Senate staffer — a room full of pink t-shirts at a hearing he'd organized for Senator Kerry, where he was caught smiling at their chants and told to keep his opinions to himself. When he was arrested, Code Pink "was right there next to me," threw his going-away party before prison, ran the sustained call campaign that helped stop his diesel-therapy transfer, stood with him through the 2019 Venezuelan embassy siege — and after prison he volunteered as coordinator of Code Pink Congress.

signature-strikes.title: National Bird
signature-strikes.summary: Award-winning documentary on the U.S. drone program featuring whistleblower Daniel Hale; John Kiriakou calls it essential viewing, noting its footage of drone operators debating on audio whether the figures in their crosshairs are children before firing.

sigurdur-thordarson.title: Julian Assange
sigurdur-thordarson.summary: Kiriakou — a 15-year friend and former WikiLeaks board member — on why Assange is a publisher owed a journalist's immunity, and a political prisoner.

sigurdur-thordarson.title: Prosecutorial careerism
sigurdur-thordarson.summary: John Kiriakou''s explanation for why senior federal prosecutors pursue high-profile national-security cases regardless of their merits: the conviction of a famous defendant is the entry ticket to a partnership at a large firm, a congressional candidacy, or a run for governor.

sigurdur-thordarson.title: Daniel Ellsberg
sigurdur-thordarson.summary: The Pentagon Papers whistleblower Kiriakou calls 'the Godfather of all national security whistleblowers' — and one of the great mentors of his life.

sigurdur-thordarson.title: Communications management unit
sigurdur-thordarson.summary: The restricted-contact units inside American medium- and maximum-security federal prisons, which John Kiriakou groups with solitary confinement as a practice that amounts to torture.

sigurdur-thordarson.title: Death threats against Kiriakou
sigurdur-thordarson.summary: The threats John Kiriakou received after going public about the CIA torture program. On FBI advice that at least two of them were credible, he took his wife and children out of the country to Mexico for a fortnight.

sigurdur-thordarson.title: Solitary confinement
sigurdur-thordarson.summary: The prison isolation practice the United Nations calls a form of torture; John Kiriakou, drawing on his own ten days in a six-by-sixteen-foot cell, argues that jailing depressed prisoners like Daniel Hale in solitary 'for their own safety' is precisely what drives them to suicide.

skip-gnehm.title: Sheikh Jaber al-Ahmad
skip-gnehm.summary: Amir of Kuwait during the 1990 Iraqi invasion and the 1991 liberation; per John Kiriakou, "a very kind and decent man and a leader who genuinely loved and cared for his people"; the subject of a CIA cable Kiriakou wrote from Taif which led President George H. W. Bush to invite the Amir to Washington for "the red carpet treatment" — after which the Amir returned with renewed focus on driving the Iraqis out.

skip-gnehm.title: Saud Nasir Al-Sabah
skip-gnehm.summary: Kuwaiti Ambassador to the United States in the run-up to the 1990 Iraqi invasion; per John Kiriakou, "just a lovely, lovely man, very generous with his time"; the diplomatic channel through which the CIA, working from the Kuwaiti embassy in Washington, communicated its escalating June–July 1990 warnings that Iraq was preparing to invade.

skip-gnehm.title: Sheikh Saad al-Abdullah
skip-gnehm.summary: Crown Prince and Prime Minister of Kuwait during the 1990–91 Iraqi occupation; per John Kiriakou, the day-to-day leader of the Kuwaiti government-in-exile in Taif — "very military," "hands-on," "the best leader Kuwait had for that situation," meeting twenty hours a day with everyone who needed to be met and simultaneously managing the Kuwaiti resistance on the ground.

skip-gnehm.title: 1993 Bush Kuwait assassination plot
skip-gnehm.summary: Iraqi intelligence plot, foiled by Kuwaiti authorities, to assassinate former President George H. W. Bush during his post-liberation "victory lap" visit to Kuwait; the U.S. response, per John Kiriakou's first-person account of his telephone call with Chairman of the Joint Chiefs Colin Powell, was 47 cruise missiles fired into the Iraqi Intelligence Service headquarters in Baghdad eight hours later.

skip-gnehm.title: Abolish the CIA
skip-gnehm.summary: John Kiriakou's position that the CIA should be abolished because its functions are already duplicated by the other 17 U.S. intelligence agencies — analysis by the State Department, human spying by the Pentagon, technology by DARPA, NSA and the private sector.

skip-gnehm.title: Ahmed Chalabi
skip-gnehm.summary: Iraqi exile and founder of the Iraqi National Congress; per John Kiriakou, a Shia-Kurdish con man who looted Petra Bank in Jordan of $36 million in the 1980s, was sentenced to death in absentia, was pardoned at CIA request, then pocketed $6 million in CIA seed funding for the INC and bought a Mayfair house in cash; later resurrected by Dick Cheney to feed the Pentagon fabricated WMD intelligence used to justify the 2003 invasion of Iraq.

sleep-deprivation.title: Enhanced interrogation techniques
sleep-deprivation.summary: The CIA's post-9/11 interrogation program; described by John Kiriakou as torture and as a euphemism designed to insulate the responsible officials from legal exposure.

sleep-deprivation.title: Donald Rumsfeld
sleep-deprivation.summary: U.S. Secretary of Defense during the post-9/11 torture program; John Kiriakou recounts Rumsfeld dismissing sleep deprivation as a real technique by pointing to his own standup desk — missing, Kiriakou says, what prolonged, forced sleeplessness actually does to prisoners.

sleep-deprivation.title: Learned Helplessness
sleep-deprivation.summary: Psychological concept adapted by the CIA as the theoretical basis for its post-9/11 enhanced interrogation program; per John Kiriakou, the goal of techniques including waterboarding was not primarily to elicit specific information but to render the prisoner so terrified of his captors that he would volunteer confessions on demand — a state of complete psychological collapse in which the prisoner loses any sense of agency or resistance.

sleep-deprivation.title: Ramzi bin al-Shibh
sleep-deprivation.summary: Alleged September 11 co-conspirator declared clinically insane by the Pentagon's psychiatrist as a result of CIA sleep deprivation; the U.S. Defense Department has stated that he cannot be tried.

sleep-deprivation.title: Robert Mueller
sleep-deprivation.summary: Director of the FBI in the years after September 11, 2001; per John Kiriakou, the official who, upon learning on July 31, 2002 that the CIA had won presidential approval to take primacy over Abu Zubaydah's interrogation away from the FBI's Ali Soufan, withdrew not just FBI personnel from the black site but every FBI employee from the country itself within 48 hours — "we know what these CIA guys are going to do; they're going to go completely nuts; we don't want any part of it."

sleep-deprivation.title: Walling
sleep-deprivation.summary: A CIA interrogation technique in which a detainee is slammed against a wall; designed on paper to use a padded fiberboard surface and a rolled towel around the neck, but applied in practice against bare concrete-block walls without protective measures, producing in at least one case permanent brain damage.

sleeper-agent.title: John Kiriakou
sleeper-agent.summary: American former CIA counterterrorism officer, whistleblower, author, and podcast host

sleeper-agent.title: MOSSAD
sleeper-agent.summary: Israel's primary external intelligence service; characterized by John Kiriakou as universally hostile in his and his CIA colleagues' professional dealings with it ("never had a positive encounter with Mossad"); operates almost exclusively in the operational rather than analytical domain; the CIA is, per Kiriakou, categorically forbidden from spying on it.

sleeper-agent.title: Asset acquisition cycle
sleeper-agent.summary: The four-step process — spot, assess, develop, recruit — taught as the first lesson of CIA case officer training

sleeper-agent.title: MK-Ultra
sleeper-agent.summary: The CIA's mid-twentieth-century umbrella program of mind-control, behavioral-modification, and biological-warfare experimentation, encompassing subprojects such as MK-Chickwit and MK-Seesaw; active 1952–1975; documented practices included LSD dosing of unwitting American citizens in CIA-rented brothels and the aerosolized release of pathogens into the San Francisco fog; 80% of the program's documentation was destroyed by the CIA in defiance of a 1975 preservation order from Senator Frank Church.

sleeper-agent.title: Surveillance detection route
sleeper-agent.summary: Tradecraft technique used by intelligence officers and assets to determine whether they are being followed before, during, or after an operational meeting

sleeper-agent.title: Dead drop
sleeper-agent.summary: The classic tradecraft technique of passing material through a hidden location rather than a meeting. Per John Kiriakou, the hard part is not the drop but everything around it — in a sophisticated counterintelligence environment, merely identifying a viable site is very difficult, and the drop itself is bracketed by surveillance detection routes of two to three hours, or eight in Russia or China. Concealments run to the ingenious: one colleague built a dead drop container inside a condom, "because who''s going to touch a condom?"

sociopathic-tendencies.title: John Kiriakou
sociopathic-tendencies.summary: American former CIA counterterrorism officer, whistleblower, author, and podcast host

sociopathic-tendencies.title: CIA Torture Program Whistleblowing
sociopathic-tendencies.summary: In December 2007, John Kiriakou became the first former CIA officer to publicly confirm the agency's post-9/11 torture program, telling ABC's Brian Ross that torture — including waterboarding — was official U.S. government policy personally approved by the president. Per Kiriakou, the decision followed a slow, incremental disillusionment dating back to a hooding incident in the field, years of waiting for someone else to come forward first, and culminated in prosecution under the Espionage Act after the program's congressional overseers publicly denied knowledge of what they had authorized and funded.

sociopathic-tendencies.title: Jeffrey Epstein
sociopathic-tendencies.summary: Convicted sex offender; per John Kiriakou, was "an Israeli access agent" rather than a CIA asset, because the CIA collects foreign intelligence and Epstein's targets — Bill Clinton, Bill Gates, Prince Andrew — were not foreign. Kiriakou further holds that Epstein did die by suicide in federal custody, because in the Bureau of Prisons the cameras never work and the guards are always asleep.

sociopathic-tendencies.title: Kiriakou's transfer to the Directorate of Operations
sociopathic-tendencies.summary: John Kiriakou's roughly two-month internal campaign to transfer from the CIA's analytic Directorate of Intelligence to the operational Directorate of Operations, overcoming what he calls a "natural bias in operations against the eggheads on the analytic side," followed by an Athens posting secured because he was the only person in the entire CIA fluent in both Greek and Arabic. Covers his full CIA career arc from 1988/1990 recruitment through analyst years on Iraq, the switch to operations, 9/11, the enhanced-interrogation refusal, executive assistant to the deputy director for operations, and his eventual resignation and post-CIA career.

sociopathic-tendencies.title: Surveillance detection route
sociopathic-tendencies.summary: Tradecraft technique used by intelligence officers and assets to determine whether they are being followed before, during, or after an operational meeting

sociopathic-tendencies.title: Gay Diplomat Operation
sociopathic-tendencies.summary: Per John Kiriakou, a CIA recruitment operation he ran against a foreign diplomat who was closeted and gay. After months of cultivation under cover as a gay man, Kiriakou attempted to kiss the diplomat at his apartment and was deflated by the response: ''I am gay. I''m just not into hairy guys.'' The romantic gambit failed — but the recruitment ultimately succeeded anyway, because the diplomat had been passed over for a promotion and was angry enough at his own government to cooperate. Kiriakou cites the operation as evidence that financial motivation and personal grievance, not coercion, are the reliable drivers of recruitment.

sofia-bulgaria-dead-drop.title: 1953 Iran coup
sofia-bulgaria-dead-drop.summary: The U.S.- and UK-backed overthrow of Iran's democratically elected prime minister, Mohammad Mossadegh; per John Kiriakou, the coup served British national interests rather than American ones, and the subsequent outlawing of secular political opposition under the Shah forced dissent into the mosques — producing a religious rather than secular revolution in 1979.

sofia-bulgaria-dead-drop.title: AIPAC
sofia-bulgaria-dead-drop.summary: The American Israel Public Affairs Committee — the U.S. political organization that, in John Kiriakou's framing, ought to be registered as a foreign-lobbying entity but is not, and that wields decisive electoral power against U.S. elected officials who express support for Palestinian human rights.

sofia-bulgaria-dead-drop.title: Barack Obama
sofia-bulgaria-dead-drop.summary: 44th U.S. president; in John Kiriakou's account, Obama publicly recounted refusing Benjamin Netanyahu's demand to bomb Iran and calling Israel's threat to use nuclear weapons a bluff — a bluff Kiriakou says Donald Trump later believed.

sofia-bulgaria-dead-drop.title: CIA adultery culture
sofia-bulgaria-dead-drop.summary: John Kiriakou's recurring characterization of the CIA officer corps as riddled with adultery and casual sex — which he frames not as gossip but as a systemic counterintelligence vulnerability that makes officers easy to recruit.

sofia-bulgaria-dead-drop.title: CIA cable priority levels
sofia-bulgaria-dead-drop.summary: The five levels of immediacy assigned to U.S. government cable traffic, as described by John Kiriakou. From lowest to highest: Routine, Priority, Immediate, Flash, CRITIC. Most career officers will never see a CRITIC; during the Gulf War, Kiriakou''s desk was receiving multiple CRITICs a day, each one announcing a hostile missile launch.

sofia-bulgaria-dead-drop.title: CIA Democrats (2016)
sofia-bulgaria-dead-drop.summary: John Kiriakou's term for a wave of 2016-era congressional candidates with intelligence or military backgrounds who ran for office opposing Trump from the right on Russia — including former CIA officer Abigail Spanberger, who won a one-term-limited Virginia governorship, and former DIA official Elissa Slotkin, who moved from intelligence into Congress and the Senate — both of whom Kiriakou suggests are positioning for future presidential runs.

solitary-confinement.title: Julian Assange
solitary-confinement.summary: Kiriakou — a 15-year friend and former WikiLeaks board member — on why Assange is a publisher owed a journalist's immunity, and a political prisoner.

solitary-confinement.title: Espionage Act
solitary-confinement.summary: United States federal law enacted in 1917, originally aimed at combating German saboteurs during World War I; per John Kiriakou, never meaningfully updated, does not mention the word 'classified information' anywhere in its text, and has been used disproportionately against national security whistleblowers — particularly under the Obama administration, which prosecuted eight people under the act for speaking to the press, nearly three times the total of all previous presidents combined.

solitary-confinement.title: RDAP program
solitary-confinement.summary: The Bureau of Prisons' Residential Drug and Alcohol Program, which can shave 12 to 18 months off a federal sentence; John Kiriakou repeatedly advises fellow whistleblowers that, combined with good behavior and a halfway house, it can turn a five-year sentence into as little as two and a half years.

solitary-confinement.title: Correctional officers at FCI Loretto
solitary-confinement.summary: Kiriakou's portraits of the staff at FCI Loretto — including two officers who tried to trick him into a fight, a lieutenant forced out of several prisons for harassment, and an officer whose abuse of prisoners he successfully reported.

solitary-confinement.title: Marty Gottesfeld
solitary-confinement.summary: American hacktivist and computer security engineer, convicted for a 2014 denial-of-service attack on Boston Children's Hospital in protest of the treatment of patient Justina Pelletier; a fellow federal prisoner of John Kiriakou who has publicly taken up the case of Donnie Reynolds Jr.

solitary-confinement.title: Prison phone monitoring
solitary-confinement.summary: Kiriakou treated the recording of his prison telephone calls as an intelligence channel rather than a constraint, planting messages for staff he knew were listening — a practice that produced a confrontation with a lieutenant over the word 'Nimrod'.

somali-land.title: Greenland
somali-land.summary: Per John Kiriakou, the U.S. is seriously pursuing acquisition of Greenland — not by force, a White House contact told him, but by leaning on a 1951/1953 treaty with Denmark to claim de facto basing and resource rights; every EU member has pledged support for Denmark, and Kiriakou warns that forcibly taking Greenland could end NATO.

somali-land.title: Jeffrey Epstein
somali-land.summary: Convicted sex offender; per John Kiriakou, was "an Israeli access agent" rather than a CIA asset, because the CIA collects foreign intelligence and Epstein's targets — Bill Clinton, Bill Gates, Prince Andrew — were not foreign. Kiriakou further holds that Epstein did die by suicide in federal custody, because in the Bureau of Prisons the cameras never work and the guards are always asleep.

somali-land.title: Mujahedin-e Khalq (MEK)
somali-land.summary: Iranian opposition group that John Kiriakou describes as 'a quasi-communist cult' and a former U.S.-designated terrorist organization. Founded by a husband-and-wife team in the 1960s and based in northeastern Iraq, the MEK launched cross-border terrorist attacks into Iran and, per Kiriakou, attempted to murder the American ambassador and the senior U.S. general in Iran — carrying out anti-American attacks for decades. After Saddam Hussein expelled them they relocated to Paris; current leader Maryam Rajavi is widely believed to have killed or had killed her vanished husband to take over. In 2009 the MEK hired high-powered Washington lobbyists (from Howard Dean to Rudy Giuliani) to get off the terrorism list, and Kiriakou says it is now funded by Israel and used as assassins-for-hire in Tehran.

somali-land.title: Bab al-Mandab
somali-land.summary: The strait where the Horn of Africa nearly meets the south-western tip of the Arabian Peninsula, which John Kiriakou identifies as one of the few American national interests in Yemen and as a chokepoint whose closure would push the global economy into recession.

somali-land.title: Hillary Clinton
somali-land.summary: Former U.S. Secretary of State and 2016 presidential candidate; John Kiriakou describes her as arguably the most neoconservative candidate Democrats could have nominated, more militarist even than her husband, and credits her — separately — with correctly describing Iran as a military dictatorship run by the IRGC rather than a genuine theocracy.

somali-land.title: Israel's cell-phone assassinations in Iran
somali-land.summary: John Kiriakou's account of how Israel wiped out Iran's military leadership by tracking cell phones — recruiting destitute Afghan refugees as $100-a-month spotters, and, when the generals stopped carrying phones, targeting their bodyguards' phones instead.

souda-bay-crete-vulnerability.title: Bashar al-Assad
souda-bay-crete-vulnerability.summary: President of Syria; John Kiriakou recounts warning Senator John Kerry to stop publicly calling Assad 'my dear friend' after a speech enraged Washington's Lebanese community, with Kerry citing motorcycle rides they had taken together to the Golan Heights.

souda-bay-crete-vulnerability.title: Benjamin Netanyahu
souda-bay-crete-vulnerability.summary: Israeli prime minister, per John Kiriakou an unpopular but politically durable figure whom Kiriakou says has spent decades pressing successive U.S. presidents to bomb Iran, presided over escalating land seizures in the West Bank, and used the October 7 attack and its aftermath to entrench his own political survival.

souda-bay-crete-vulnerability.title: Bob Baer
souda-bay-crete-vulnerability.summary: Former CIA case officer; per John Kiriakou, "pretty famous"; the subject of George Clooney's film Syriana; pulled out of northern Iraq by the Clinton White House in the 1990s after [NSA intercepted](/wiki/the-intercept) a communication revealing he was developing a network of sources to assassinate Saddam Hussein — National Security Adviser Sandy Berger called CIA and threatened him with a conspiracy charge.

souda-bay-crete-vulnerability.title: China as economic threat
souda-bay-crete-vulnerability.summary: John Kiriakou's argument that China is the real threat to the West not militarily — it has one aircraft carrier to America's two dozen and rarely invades — but economically, buying friends worldwide while the U.S. spends a trillion dollars a year on weapons.

souda-bay-crete-vulnerability.title: Donald Trump
souda-bay-crete-vulnerability.summary: 45th and 47th U.S. president. Per John Kiriakou, a man genuinely convinced he was doing right by bombing Iran, "duped" by the same Netanyahu nuclear bluff Obama once rejected — and, at the same time, the most blindly pro-Israel president in history, an admirer of autocrats who has never once criticized Vladimir Putin, and prone to gestures — from the Gulf of America to a since-abandoned "Department of War" rename — that test the edges of his actual authority.

souda-bay-crete-vulnerability.title: Hamas
souda-bay-crete-vulnerability.summary: The Palestinian movement behind the October 7, 2023 attack; John Kiriakou argues that a case could be made for calling it a freedom-fighting organization dedicated to the liberation of its people rather than simply a terrorist group, notes it is labeled a terrorist organization by only a small minority of UN member states, and has ruled Gaza since Israel's 2005 withdrawal.

south-caucasus-realignment.title: Iran regional war (2026)
south-caucasus-realignment.summary: The widening of the 2026 Iran conflict from a war between Iran on one side and the United States and Israel on the other into a regional war — Iranian missiles striking a US base in Jordan, Iranian strikes across the Gulf states, Houthi attacks on Saudi shipping and oil, and Saudi forces striking pro-Iranian militias in Iraq. John Kiriakou notes he had forecast the expansion a week earlier.

south-caucasus-realignment.title: Israel, Turkey, and NATO Article 5
south-caucasus-realignment.summary: John Kiriakou's scenario in which an Israeli attack on Turkey would oblige every NATO member, the United States included, to come to Turkey's defence — and in which the alliance would sooner dissolve than honour that obligation against Israel.

south-caucasus-realignment.title: Israeli drone factories in Serbia
south-caucasus-realignment.summary: Five drone factories John Kiriakou was told the Israelis are building in Serbia — a fact relayed to him by members of a Serbian delegation who welcomed it on the grounds that Israel is effective against Islamists, and which Kiriakou treats as the same emotional play he sees used on Greeks and Cypriots.

south-caucasus-realignment.title: Israeli property acquisition in Greece and Cyprus
south-caucasus-realignment.summary: John Kiriakou's account of Israelis buying land in Greece and Cyprus at a scale he considers destabilising — entire villages rather than holiday homes, a Jewish-only village outside Paphos with a casino attached, a rejected bid for an island in the Ionian Sea, and a request to open the first Zionist high school in Cyprus.

south-caucasus-realignment.title: Antisemitism and anti-Zionism
south-caucasus-realignment.summary: The conflation of criticism of the Israeli state with hatred of Jews, which John Kiriakou describes as a worldwide confusion and, according to a young Israeli he spoke to, an explicit lesson of the Israeli school system; a subject Kiriakou says he personally struggles with.

south-caucasus-realignment.title: Benjamin Netanyahu
south-caucasus-realignment.summary: Israeli prime minister, per John Kiriakou an unpopular but politically durable figure whom Kiriakou says has spent decades pressing successive U.S. presidents to bomb Iran, presided over escalating land seizures in the West Bank, and used the October 7 attack and its aftermath to entrench his own political survival.

soviet-union.title: Cold War
soviet-union.summary: The U.S.–Soviet confrontation that built the CIA John Kiriakou joined. Kiriakou argues the Cold War was real "but also at a certain level desired" — America has always needed an ism to oppose — and that its habits never died: "The Russians thought the Cold War was over, but no one told the US." From its memoirs he draws a standing tradecraft lesson (the CIA''s best recruits were always walk-ins), and in the new Russia and China confrontations he sees a Cold War 2.0 rebuilt on the old exaggerations.

soviet-union.title: Central Intelligence Agency
soviet-union.summary: U.S. foreign intelligence service; John Kiriakou's employer from 1990 to 2004 and the central institution of KiriPedia

soviet-union.title: MOSSAD
soviet-union.summary: Israel's primary external intelligence service; characterized by John Kiriakou as universally hostile in his and his CIA colleagues' professional dealings with it ("never had a positive encounter with Mossad"); operates almost exclusively in the operational rather than analytical domain; the CIA is, per Kiriakou, categorically forbidden from spying on it.

soviet-union.title: Afghan heroin policy
soviet-union.summary: The post-2001 U.S. policy in Afghanistan of protecting, and per John Kiriakou actively encouraging, the cultivation of heroin poppy. Under the Taliban in 2000 Afghanistan produced 0% of the world's heroin; by 2009 under American occupation it produced 93%. Per a DEA officer Kiriakou consulted with on the policy paper he was preparing for Senator Kerry, the strategic rationale was that nearly all of the heroin flowed to Iran and Russia, addiction in those countries was considered desirable as a long-run societal weakener, and the same logic now operates in reverse with Chinese fentanyl flowing into the United States.

soviet-union.title: CIA Torture Program Whistleblowing
soviet-union.summary: In December 2007, John Kiriakou became the first former CIA officer to publicly confirm the agency's post-9/11 torture program, telling ABC's Brian Ross that torture — including waterboarding — was official U.S. government policy personally approved by the president. Per Kiriakou, the decision followed a slow, incremental disillusionment dating back to a hooding incident in the field, years of waiting for someone else to come forward first, and culminated in prosecution under the Espionage Act after the program's congressional overseers publicly denied knowledge of what they had authorized and funded.

soviet-union.title: Edward Snowden
soviet-union.summary: Former NSA contractor who in 2013 disclosed the scope of U.S. [mass surveillance](/wiki/mass-surveillance), including the Section 702 collection program. Per John Kiriakou — who counts Snowden among the small group of national-security whistleblowers prosecuted under the Espionage Act — Snowden was ''stuck between two awful slippery slopes'': breaking his oath and chain of command on one side, and on the other catching something ''cut and dry against the Constitution'' that no one would act on. Kiriakou notes Snowden could not use his chain of command (as Kiriakou could not, his own chain being Jose Rodriguez), and that Judge Leonie Brinkema had reserved the Snowden case for herself before he fled the country.

soylent-green-cable-easter-egg.title: Central Intelligence Agency
soylent-green-cable-easter-egg.summary: U.S. foreign intelligence service; John Kiriakou's employer from 1990 to 2004 and the central institution of KiriPedia

soylent-green-cable-easter-egg.title: Asset acquisition cycle
soylent-green-cable-easter-egg.summary: The four-step process — spot, assess, develop, recruit — taught as the first lesson of CIA case officer training

soylent-green-cable-easter-egg.title: Pick the man, then find the crime
soylent-green-cable-easter-egg.summary: Robert H. Jackson's 1940 doctrine — recurringly invoked by John Kiriakou — that a prosecutor's worst abuse is to select a target and then comb the law books for an offense to charge him with

soylent-green-cable-easter-egg.title: 2026 Iran war
soylent-green-cable-easter-egg.summary: The open-ended American and Israeli war against Iran that John Kiriakou tracked week by week on his own show — a conflict he says was sold as three weeks, ran into its fifth month, achieved every decapitation objective it set, and continued anyway. His grade for it is a D, and his forecast is a Truth Social post declaring victory while nothing changes.

soylent-green-cable-easter-egg.title: Abu Zubaydah
soylent-green-cable-easter-egg.summary: Detainee captured by John Kiriakou's CIA team in Pakistan in March 2002; the first subject of the agency's enhanced interrogation techniques program; subjected to both approved and unauthorized techniques including the cockroach-in-coffin treatment exploiting a documented insect phobia.

soylent-green-cable-easter-egg.title: Adnan Khashoggi
soylent-green-cable-easter-egg.summary: Saudi arms dealer and Iran-Contra middleman whom John Kiriakou says was mentioned 'all the time' at the CIA — in pointed contrast to Jeffrey Epstein, whose name he never once heard there.

special-activities-division.title: Tuesday morning kill list
special-activities-division.summary: Weekly CIA targeting meeting instituted by John Brennan in 2009 during his service as Deputy National Security Advisor for Counterterrorism in the Obama administration; produced a written list of individuals to be killed in the following week; per John Kiriakou, the program was a source of pride within the Obama administration and was made operationally possible by the targeting-software sophistication of the period.

special-activities-division.title: Ground Branch
special-activities-division.summary: The land-operating component of the CIA's Special Activities Division; the unit whose secrecy and personnel composition — predominantly former SEAL Team 6 and Delta Force operators on secondment to the agency — gave the 2025 Dalton Fischer Podcast episode its subtitle, "The Most Secret CIA Unit."

special-activities-division.title: Jack Murphy NATO Sabotage Story
special-activities-division.summary: John Kiriakou's account of a story reported by podcaster Jack Murphy — over a year in the making, drawing on CIA and Army intelligence sources — alleging the CIA worked through a NATO partner to conduct sabotage inside Russia, including munitions-warehouse fires and rail explosions; killed before publication after the CIA deputy director denied it on a call with the editor and blamed "rogue Ukrainians."

special-activities-division.title: Hamilton 68
special-activities-division.summary: A company founded by former CIA, FBI, NSA and Director of National Intelligence officials that rates news sites as reliable or unreliable, contracting mainly with the Pentagon to flag articles on government computers with green or red check marks; John Kiriakou says it threatened Consortium News with a "Kremlin apologist" red-check designation, after which PayPal permanently suspended the outlet's account and confiscated its funds.

special-activities-division.title: Pan Quake
special-activities-division.summary: An open-source, nonprofit, carbon-neutral social media platform based in Iceland and powered by geothermal energy, incorporated with lawyers in Luxembourg; John Kiriakou was asked to serve as a brand ambassador before its Icelandic bank account was frozen at the FBI's request over the platform's association with Julian Assange supporters.

special-activities-division.title: Shin Bet
special-activities-division.summary: Israel's internal security service; per John Kiriakou, one of the two declared Israeli intelligence officers at the Washington embassy, and the service whose officer, alongside a Mossad officer, he says tried to recruit him at his first CIA liaison briefing.

splc-2025-indictment.title: FISA
splc-2025-indictment.summary: The Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act, the U.S. legal framework governing surveillance warrants for foreign-intelligence purposes. Per John Kiriakou, FISA is dangerously easy to abuse — he cites Carter Page, whose life was ruined and who was driven into bankruptcy after the Steele dossier was used to support four FISA applications against him. Kiriakou groups FISA with the Patriot Act and Section 702 as the legal architecture stripping Americans of constitutional protections, opposed by only a handful of legislators.

splc-2025-indictment.title: Hillary Clinton
splc-2025-indictment.summary: Former U.S. Secretary of State and 2016 presidential candidate; John Kiriakou describes her as arguably the most neoconservative candidate Democrats could have nominated, more militarist even than her husband, and credits her — separately — with correctly describing Iran as a military dictatorship run by the IRGC rather than a genuine theocracy.

splc-2025-indictment.title: John Kerry
splc-2025-indictment.summary: U.S. Senator from Massachusetts; chairman of the Senate Foreign Relations Committee during John Kiriakou's 2009 service as the committee's senior investigator; subsequently U.S. Secretary of State; characterized by Kiriakou as a coward who buckled under CIA pressure on the Dasht-i-Leili reopening and as personally fixated on his perceived theft of the Secretary of State position by Hillary Clinton; the famously thrown medals were duplicates purchased at the post exchange.

splc-2025-indictment.title: John Kiriakou
splc-2025-indictment.summary: American former CIA counterterrorism officer, whistleblower, author, and podcast host

splc-2025-indictment.title: Reza Pahlavi
splc-2025-indictment.summary: The exiled Iranian crown prince whom John Kiriakou dismisses as an Israeli-backed fantasy candidate to rule Iran — a man who has not lived there since his teens, supported mainly by Beverly Hills exiles, whom Kiriakou says 'wouldn't survive the walk from the plane to the terminal.'

splc-2025-indictment.title: Barack Obama
splc-2025-indictment.summary: 44th U.S. president; in John Kiriakou's account, Obama publicly recounted refusing Benjamin Netanyahu's demand to bomb Iran and calling Israel's threat to use nuclear weapons a bluff — a bluff Kiriakou says Donald Trump later believed.

spy-films-accuracy.title: The spy shop
spy-films-accuracy.summary: A London shop with a New York sister branch where, John Kiriakou says, the CIA bought a good deal of the equipment it needed, on the reasoning that a thousand-dollar purchase beat a million-dollar development programme.

spy-films-accuracy.title: Surveillance detection route
spy-films-accuracy.summary: Tradecraft technique used by intelligence officers and assets to determine whether they are being followed before, during, or after an operational meeting

spy-films-accuracy.title: Abu Zubaydah
spy-films-accuracy.summary: Detainee captured by John Kiriakou's CIA team in Pakistan in March 2002; the first subject of the agency's enhanced interrogation techniques program; subjected to both approved and unauthorized techniques including the cockroach-in-coffin treatment exploiting a documented insect phobia.

spy-films-accuracy.title: Benjamin Netanyahu
spy-films-accuracy.summary: Israeli prime minister, per John Kiriakou an unpopular but politically durable figure whom Kiriakou says has spent decades pressing successive U.S. presidents to bomb Iran, presided over escalating land seizures in the West Bank, and used the October 7 attack and its aftermath to entrench his own political survival.

spy-films-accuracy.title: Bureau of Prisons advisory board
spy-films-accuracy.summary: The advisory board John Kiriakou joined at the personal invitation of the Director of the Bureau of Prisons, who told him the president had tasked him with tearing the Bureau down and rebuilding it.

spy-films-accuracy.title: The Green Line in Nicosia
spy-films-accuracy.summary: The division of Nicosia between the Republic of Cyprus and the Turkish-occupied north, which John Kiriakou toured in July 2026 and described as maintained through deliberate humiliation rather than any interest in settlement.

st-nectarios-of-aegina.title: Greek Intelligence Service
st-nectarios-of-aegina.summary: Greece's intelligence service, with which John Kiriakou worked closely during his Athens posting; its head of surveillance called off surveillance on him after watching him make a large offering at Saint Nectarios's tomb on the island of Aegina.

st-nectarios-of-aegina.title: John Kiriakou
st-nectarios-of-aegina.summary: American former CIA counterterrorism officer, whistleblower, author, and podcast host

st-nectarios-of-aegina.title: Church of Saint Porphyrios
st-nectarios-of-aegina.summary: The Greek Orthodox church in Gaza that John Kiriakou describes as the oldest continuously operating church in the world; per Kiriakou, Israel bombed it while 24 women and children were sheltering inside.

st-nectarios-of-aegina.title: Seyyed Hossein Nasr
st-nectarios-of-aegina.summary: The scholar of Islamic philosophy under whom John Kiriakou studied Shiism as an undergraduate. Kiriakou calls him probably the most important Shia Muslim scholar in the world, notes that he is the father of Vali Nasr, and remarks that at ninety-eight he is still teaching.

st-nectarios-of-aegina.title: Benjamin Netanyahu
st-nectarios-of-aegina.summary: Israeli prime minister, per John Kiriakou an unpopular but politically durable figure whom Kiriakou says has spent decades pressing successive U.S. presidents to bomb Iran, presided over escalating land seizures in the West Bank, and used the October 7 attack and its aftermath to entrench his own political survival.

st-nectarios-of-aegina.title: CIA Torture Program Whistleblowing
st-nectarios-of-aegina.summary: In December 2007, John Kiriakou became the first former CIA officer to publicly confirm the agency's post-9/11 torture program, telling ABC's Brian Ross that torture — including waterboarding — was official U.S. government policy personally approved by the president. Per Kiriakou, the decision followed a slow, incremental disillusionment dating back to a hooding incident in the field, years of waiting for someone else to come forward first, and culminated in prosecution under the Espionage Act after the program's congressional overseers publicly denied knowledge of what they had authorized and funded.

st-porphyrios-church-gaza.title: Benjamin Netanyahu
st-porphyrios-church-gaza.summary: Israeli prime minister, per John Kiriakou an unpopular but politically durable figure whom Kiriakou says has spent decades pressing successive U.S. presidents to bomb Iran, presided over escalating land seizures in the West Bank, and used the October 7 attack and its aftermath to entrench his own political survival.

st-porphyrios-church-gaza.title: Taybeh
st-porphyrios-church-gaza.summary: The only fully Christian village in the West Bank, home to the Holy Land's oldest brewery; John Kiriakou recounts it being set on fire and its Marian festival attacked by the IDF with drones, helicopters and stun grenades.

st-porphyrios-church-gaza.title: Shireen Abu Akleh
st-porphyrios-church-gaza.summary: Al Jazeera journalist, U.S. citizen and Greek Orthodox Christian; John Kiriakou recounts that she was shot in the face by an Israeli sniper while wearing clearly marked press gear, and that the IDF then beat pallbearers at her funeral.

st-porphyrios-church-gaza.title: Mount Weather
st-porphyrios-church-gaza.summary: U.S. government continuity-of-government underground facility on the Virginia–West Virginia line

st-porphyrios-church-gaza.title: Jerry Falwell Jr.
st-porphyrios-church-gaza.summary: Evangelical leader and former president of Liberty University; John Kiriakou recounts that Falwell personally recruited him to lecture at Liberty's Jesse Helms School of Government after his whistleblowing, with the reasoning that "torture is not Christian."

st-porphyrios-church-gaza.title: King Abdullah II of Jordan
st-porphyrios-church-gaza.summary: The Jordanian monarch whom John Kiriakou rates as knowing more about the Middle East than anyone else who leads or studies it, and as almost never wrong across twenty-five years of foreign-policy predictions. Kiriakou recounts the deathbed succession that made him king against his own expectations, and his refusal after October 7 to accept Palestinian refugees on the grounds that doing so would deliver Israel the ethnic cleansing it wanted.

stephen-saunders.title: John Kiriakou
stephen-saunders.summary: American former CIA counterterrorism officer, whistleblower, author, and podcast host

stephen-saunders.title: Revolutionary Organization 17 November
stephen-saunders.summary: Greek far-left urban guerrilla group active 1975–2002; the deadliest terrorist organization in Greek history

stephen-saunders.title: CIA Torture Program Whistleblowing
stephen-saunders.summary: In December 2007, John Kiriakou became the first former CIA officer to publicly confirm the agency's post-9/11 torture program, telling ABC's Brian Ross that torture — including waterboarding — was official U.S. government policy personally approved by the president. Per Kiriakou, the decision followed a slow, incremental disillusionment dating back to a hooding incident in the field, years of waiting for someone else to come forward first, and culminated in prosecution under the Espionage Act after the program's congressional overseers publicly denied knowledge of what they had authorized and funded.

stephen-saunders.title: The Welch .45
stephen-saunders.summary: The single .45 caliber pistol used by Revolutionary Organization 17 November in every confirmed assassination over the group's twenty-seven-year operational life

stephen-saunders.title: Carlos the Jackal
stephen-saunders.summary: Venezuelan-born militant (Ilich Ramírez Sánchez) active in the 1970s and 1980s; per John Kiriakou, 'the Osama bin Laden of the 70s and 80s.' Kiriakou spent his Athens posting trying to identify the middleman linking Carlos to the Greek terrorist group 17 November, then six months working the lead with MI5 in London; Carlos was finally run down by CIA contractor Billy Waugh in a Khartoum vegetable market and captured in 1994.

stephen-saunders.title: Heather Saunders
stephen-saunders.summary: Widow of British Brigadier General Stephen Saunders, the British defense attaché in Athens assassinated by Revolutionary Organization 17 November on April 22, 2000; per John Kiriakou, the person whose post-assassination Greek-television statement — "this organization is not a political organization nor is it a phantom group; it's a gang of criminals" — for the first time since 17 November's 1975 founding turned Greek public opinion against the group.

steve-kappes.title: Yemen
steve-kappes.summary: Country on the southern Arabian Peninsula; setting of five John Kiriakou trips between 1990 and approximately 2010, spanning the country's brief unification, its civil war, and its present condition as a high-threat operating environment for U.S. and allied diplomatic personnel.

steve-kappes.title: Abu Zubaydah
steve-kappes.summary: Detainee captured by John Kiriakou's CIA team in Pakistan in March 2002; the first subject of the agency's enhanced interrogation techniques program; subjected to both approved and unauthorized techniques including the cockroach-in-coffin treatment exploiting a documented insect phobia.

steve-kappes.title: AIPAC
steve-kappes.summary: The American Israel Public Affairs Committee — the U.S. political organization that, in John Kiriakou's framing, ought to be registered as a foreign-lobbying entity but is not, and that wields decisive electoral power against U.S. elected officials who express support for Palestinian human rights.

steve-kappes.title: Barack Obama
steve-kappes.summary: 44th U.S. president; in John Kiriakou's account, Obama publicly recounted refusing Benjamin Netanyahu's demand to bomb Iran and calling Israel's threat to use nuclear weapons a bluff — a bluff Kiriakou says Donald Trump later believed.

steve-kappes.title: Bilderberg and weapon sales
steve-kappes.summary: John Kiriakou's claim, sourced to someone he knew who attended, that elite gatherings like Bilderberg and the Shangri-La Dialogue are — beneath the talk of global issues — fundamentally 'all about weapon sales' and defense-contractor deals.

steve-kappes.title: Church Committee
steve-kappes.summary: U.S. Senate investigative committee operating in 1975–1976 that examined domestic intelligence abuses by the CIA, FBI, and NSA; per John Kiriakou, the Church Committee — alongside the concurrent Pike Committee in the House — was the last genuine moment of legislative oversight over the intelligence community, born of a national consensus that government had gone dangerously off course. Its work led to the creation of the permanent Senate Select Committee on Intelligence, which Kiriakou says ceased to function as real oversight roughly seven years after its founding.

steven-lalas.title: Greek Intelligence Service
steven-lalas.summary: Greece's intelligence service, with which John Kiriakou worked closely during his Athens posting; its head of surveillance called off surveillance on him after watching him make a large offering at Saint Nectarios's tomb on the island of Aegina.

steven-lalas.title: Aldrich Ames
steven-lalas.summary: Senior CIA officer — a GS-15 who rose to chief of counterintelligence for the Soviet branch — who spied for the KGB. Per John Kiriakou, Ames's first act of betrayal was selling the identities of two CIA agents to the Russians for $50,000 to pay off a credit-card debt; both agents were immediately executed. He ultimately caused the deaths of twelve people, accumulated $2 million, bought a house in Arlington for that amount, drove a Jaguar to work on a $70,000 salary, and built an in-ground pool with a gazebo — all while being known throughout the office as a daily drunk. A 27-year-old officer sat on the initial security file for eighteen months. Analyst Sandy Grimes ultimately caught him.

steven-lalas.title: Bahrain fishing officer demarche
steven-lalas.summary: Kiriakou's account of serving, while stationed in Bahrain, as the embassy's econ officer and by extension its fishing, banking, aviation, and environment officer — including delivering a formal U.S. demarche to Bahrain's deputy foreign minister over a U.S.-Canada dispute about whether clams legally count as fish.

steven-lalas.title: Beirut
steven-lalas.summary: The Lebanese capital John Kiriakou confirms was a genuine espionage playground — though he dates the peak to the 1950s through the mid-1970s, when Beirut was the Paris and the banking centre of the Middle East, and when, beneath the CIA, KGB and Israeli presence, "more secretly the French ran the place." He also explains why the enormous new American embassy there is about fortification rather than a regional CIA headquarters.

steven-lalas.title: Below World's End
steven-lalas.summary: Film in which John Kiriakou made his acting debut, filmed entirely in Mexico during October 2025; Kiriakou's performance earned him a Screen Actors Guild membership card, and Sean Penn told him after a private screening that he had unknowingly been acting throughout his entire CIA career.

steven-lalas.title: Big Assawoman Bay NASA launch
steven-lalas.summary: John Kiriakou's account of being taken, as a junior CIA analyst, to watch a NASA rocket launch near the village of Big Assawoman on Virginia's Eastern Shore, where he was startled to find foreign space-agency officials present unsupervised.

strait-of-hormuz-transit-fees.title: Al-Qaeda training manual interrogation-resistance tactics
strait-of-hormuz-transit-fees.summary: A captured al-Qaeda training manual instructing operatives on how to resist interrogation, including feigning illness — a technique John Kiriakou says he saw a detainee use, and recognized, during a capture and interrogation in Pakistan.

strait-of-hormuz-transit-fees.title: Djibouti
strait-of-hormuz-transit-fees.summary: John Kiriakou's observations on Djibouti — Camp Lemonnier, once split by a fence between an American and a French base, now divided between an American side and a Chinese side; and the country's tiny intelligence service, whose entire director's office, Kiriakou says, was smaller than his own rental townhouse living room.

strait-of-hormuz-transit-fees.title: CIA and the UFO question
strait-of-hormuz-transit-fees.summary: John Kiriakou's consistent answer that UFOs and alien technology are a Pentagon matter, not a CIA one — though he says nearly every former fighter-pilot friend of his has seen something inexplicable, sometimes emerging from the ocean.

strait-of-hormuz-transit-fees.title: Guantanamo Bay
strait-of-hormuz-transit-fees.summary: U.S. naval base in Cuba; site of CIA detention operations during the post-9/11 enhanced interrogation program; briefly served by John Kiriakou as interim Chief during the summer of 2002.

strait-of-hormuz-transit-fees.title: Iran 12-Day War
strait-of-hormuz-transit-fees.summary: 2025 Israeli air campaign against Iran during which Israel killed at least fourteen Iranian nuclear scientists by destroying the apartment buildings they lived in; preceded for each scientist by Farsi-language telephone calls from Iranian-Jewish Mossad and Shin Bet officers offering defection in lieu of certain death; characterized by John Kiriakou as a categorical departure from CIA targeting doctrine in its acceptable-civilian-casualty calculus.

strait-of-hormuz-transit-fees.title: Irish intelligence services
strait-of-hormuz-transit-fees.summary: Ireland's intelligence and law-enforcement services, which John Kiriakou toured and met with during a speaking trip to Belfast, Cork, Dublin, and Waterford. Per Kiriakou, Irish intelligence and the Garda are especially strong at anti-money-laundering investigation and counterterrorism — the latter traced, he says, to the large number of Irish militants trained by Carlos the Jackal in Libya and Lebanon during the 1970s.

strait-of-hormuz.title: 2026 Iran war
strait-of-hormuz.summary: The open-ended American and Israeli war against Iran that John Kiriakou tracked week by week on his own show — a conflict he says was sold as three weeks, ran into its fifth month, achieved every decapitation objective it set, and continued anyway. His grade for it is a D, and his forecast is a Truth Social post declaring victory while nothing changes.

strait-of-hormuz.title: Lindsey Graham
strait-of-hormuz.summary: Republican senator from South Carolina who died in July 2026, and John Kiriakou's standing shorthand for the permanent war caucus — a "show horse" rather than a workhorse, a "chameleon" who "never saw a war that he didn't want to jump into with both feet," and, on posthumously released documentary footage, a man offering the US Air Force to bomb a country America was not at war with.

strait-of-hormuz.title: Abraham Accords
strait-of-hormuz.summary: The Trump-brokered normalization deals between Israel and Gulf Arab states — in John Kiriakou's judgment "a terrible idea in the first place," a great victory for Israel and the Gulf Arabs that was "a punch in the throat to the Palestinians." He argues the Accords are how Trump meant to "solve the Middle East in a day" — by screwing the Palestinians — that Hamas read the abandonment correctly, that October 7 shattered the project, and that reviving the Accords (Saudis in, victory declared, Nobel collected) remains the organizing goal of Trump's regional policy.

strait-of-hormuz.title: Benjamin Netanyahu
strait-of-hormuz.summary: Israeli prime minister, per John Kiriakou an unpopular but politically durable figure whom Kiriakou says has spent decades pressing successive U.S. presidents to bomb Iran, presided over escalating land seizures in the West Bank, and used the October 7 attack and its aftermath to entrench his own political survival.

strait-of-hormuz.title: John Kiriakou's Briefing Room
strait-of-hormuz.summary: A twice-weekly news and commentary programme launched by John Kiriakou in July 2026, presented as analysis rather than partisan opinion, and distinct from his storytelling podcast Dead Drop.

strait-of-hormuz.title: Expulsion of Palestinians from the Gulf
strait-of-hormuz.summary: The mass expulsion of the Palestinian professional class from the Gulf Arab states in the aftermath of Iraq's 1990 invasion of Kuwait, which John Kiriakou witnessed from the region and identifies as the reason Gulf governments are willing to normalise relations with Israel.

strawberry-fields.title: Guantanamo Bay
strawberry-fields.summary: U.S. naval base in Cuba; site of CIA detention operations during the post-9/11 enhanced interrogation program; briefly served by John Kiriakou as interim Chief during the summer of 2002.

strawberry-fields.title: Senate Torture Report
strawberry-fields.summary: The December 2014 executive summary of the U.S. Senate Select Committee on Intelligence's study of the CIA's post-9/11 detention and interrogation program; the first public disclosure of techniques including rectal feeding with hummus, sexual assault with broomsticks, and prolonged sleep deprivation.

strawberry-fields.title: Hummus
strawberry-fields.summary: The CIA's coercive 'rectal feeding' of detainees using pureed hummus — an unauthorized interrogation technique used at post-9/11 black sites, exposed in the 2014 Senate Torture Report, and the abuse for which John Kiriakou became most associated in popular culture.

strawberry-fields.title: Enhanced interrogation techniques
strawberry-fields.summary: The CIA's post-9/11 interrogation program; described by John Kiriakou as torture and as a euphemism designed to insulate the responsible officials from legal exposure.

strawberry-fields.title: Sleep deprivation
strawberry-fields.summary: A CIA interrogation technique used against high-value detainees post-9/11; the agency was authorized to deny prisoners sleep for up to 12 days continuously; people died; at least one detainee was rendered permanently clinically insane.

strawberry-fields.title: CIA Torture Program Whistleblowing
strawberry-fields.summary: In December 2007, John Kiriakou became the first former CIA officer to publicly confirm the agency's post-9/11 torture program, telling ABC's Brian Ross that torture — including waterboarding — was official U.S. government policy personally approved by the president. Per Kiriakou, the decision followed a slow, incremental disillusionment dating back to a hooding incident in the field, years of waiting for someone else to come forward first, and culminated in prosecution under the Espionage Act after the program's congressional overseers publicly denied knowledge of what they had authorized and funded.

superdelegates.title: Tulsi Gabbard
superdelegates.summary: U.S. Director of National Intelligence; a longtime family friend of John Kiriakou's, who has known her since she was 12; Kiriakou calls her appointment "an inspired choice" despite disagreeing with her decision to join the Republican Party, and says she appears to have given up her opposition to Section 702 surveillance to secure Senate confirmation.

superdelegates.title: George McGovern
superdelegates.summary: The 1972 Democratic presidential nominee, whose landslide defeat John Kiriakou identifies as the pretext for creating superdelegates. As a George Washington University sophomore in 1983, Kiriakou wrote to McGovern offering the campus theater for a campaign launch; McGovern telephoned him personally, announced his 1984 candidacy there, and afterwards took him home for tuna sandwiches made by his wife.

superdelegates.title: 9/11 plea agreements
superdelegates.summary: The Biden-era plea deals under which Khalid Sheikh Mohammed and co-defendants agreed to plead guilty to murdering 2,976 people in exchange for life without parole and a guarantee against transfer to the Colorado supermax — vacated by the Secretary of Defense after public backlash. Per John Kiriakou, the deals existed because torture had rendered every confession inadmissible, leaving no usable evidence.

superdelegates.title: AIPAC and foreign-agent registration
superdelegates.summary: John Kiriakou's argument that AIPAC is the only organization of its kind exempt from registering under the Foreign Agents Registration Act — set against his own experience around 2008, when a contract worth five or six thousand dollars to write four op-eds praising the Abu Dhabi Chamber of Commerce obliged him to register as a foreign agent.

superdelegates.title: Guantánamo Bay detention camp
superdelegates.summary: Per John Kiriakou — as chief of counterterrorism operations in Pakistan after September 11, 2001 — the Guantanamo detention facility began as a temporary holding measure intended to last two to three weeks while the CIA and Justice Department determined which federal district court should try each prisoner, not as a long-term detention infrastructure. The Rawalpindi jail had reached capacity, Pakistani intelligence demanded the prisoners be removed, and CIA headquarters directed Kiriakou to load them onto a C-12 cargo plane and fly them to Cuba.

superdelegates.title: Iraq War Israeli tower sabotage
superdelegates.summary: Per John Kiriakou, after the U.S. rejected Israel's request to join the coalition for the Iraq War in late 2002/early 2003 — fearing the loss of Jordanian, Egyptian, and Saudi cooperation — communications towers across the western Iraqi desert began being toppled by explosives; when the New York Times asked the CIA if Israel was responsible, the agency denied any Israeli involvement.

surveillance-detection-route.title: Marriott double-agent trap
surveillance-detection-route.summary: Operation in which John Kiriakou, posing as a CIA station chief in a Middle East posting, lured a hostile-service-controlled double agent ordered to kill him into a Marriott Hotel room, tackled him out of the bathroom, sedated him with Demerol, and smuggled him out under a sheet on a gurney. A children's-style hand-drawn map with an X led the CIA to the terrorist network's full weapons cache.

surveillance-detection-route.title: The false volunteer
surveillance-detection-route.summary: A walk-in at an American embassy who claimed access to a high-priority target, was placed under surveillance and found to be a restaurant dishwasher, and whom John Kiriakou deliberately intimidated into never approaching an American embassy again.

surveillance-detection-route.title: Dead drop
surveillance-detection-route.summary: The classic tradecraft technique of passing material through a hidden location rather than a meeting. Per John Kiriakou, the hard part is not the drop but everything around it — in a sophisticated counterintelligence environment, merely identifying a viable site is very difficult, and the drop itself is bracketed by surveillance detection routes of two to three hours, or eight in Russia or China. Concealments run to the ingenious: one colleague built a dead drop container inside a condom, "because who''s going to touch a condom?"

surveillance-detection-route.title: Mad minute
surveillance-detection-route.summary: CIA case-officer procedure for the opening seconds of every meeting with a recruited source — confirm the source is safe, confirm a clean surveillance-detection route, and set the next meeting — so that if the door is kicked in, the operational essentials have already been taken care of.

surveillance-detection-route.title: Mahmud (alias)
surveillance-detection-route.summary: Pseudonym for an Egyptian al-Qaeda fighter recruited by John Kiriakou in an unnamed country during the early 2000s

surveillance-detection-route.title: Operating Directive
surveillance-detection-route.summary: The CIA's six-tier (0 through 5) intelligence priority system used to indicate the urgency with which case officers should pursue specific topics

sweat-lodge.title: The Reluctant Spy
sweat-lodge.summary: John Kiriakou''s 2009 memoir, The Reluctant Spy: My Secret Life in the CIA''s War on Terror, begun in secret months before he blew the whistle and reaching number five on the New York Times bestseller list.

sweat-lodge.title: Albert Stubblebine
sweat-lodge.summary: Per John Kiriakou, General Albert "Bert" Stubblebine was among the Army Intelligence figures behind the original Project Stargate remote-viewing program; Kiriakou interviewed the program's top people and says Stubblebine, like remote viewer Lyn Buchanan, had to sign non-disclosure agreements with the NSA and CIA.

sweat-lodge.title: Bay Path University
sweat-lodge.summary: Per John Kiriakou, he teaches in the graduate intelligence-studies program at Bay Path University in Massachusetts, covering introduction to intelligence, the history of terrorism, and intelligence and cybersecurity.

sweat-lodge.title: Espionage Act
sweat-lodge.summary: United States federal law enacted in 1917, originally aimed at combating German saboteurs during World War I; per John Kiriakou, never meaningfully updated, does not mention the word 'classified information' anywhere in its text, and has been used disproportionately against national security whistleblowers — particularly under the Obama administration, which prosecuted eight people under the act for speaking to the press, nearly three times the total of all previous presidents combined.

sweat-lodge.title: Ilhan Omar
sweat-lodge.summary: U.S. Representative whom John Kiriakou credits with sponsoring a rewrite of the Espionage Act in two consecutive Congresses — legislation he says is dead on arrival with a Republican House because of who she is.

sweat-lodge.title: Lynn Buchanan
sweat-lodge.summary: A Fort Meade-trained Army intelligence veteran of the CIA and NSA remote-viewing programs — a primary source, Kiriakou says, not a TV psychic.

taliban-embassy-raid.title: Abu Zubaydah
taliban-embassy-raid.summary: Detainee captured by John Kiriakou's CIA team in Pakistan in March 2002; the first subject of the agency's enhanced interrogation techniques program; subjected to both approved and unauthorized techniques including the cockroach-in-coffin treatment exploiting a documented insect phobia.

taliban-embassy-raid.title: Counterterrorism Center
taliban-embassy-raid.summary: The CIA's Counterterrorism Center (CTC) — the unit where John Kiriakou spent the defining years of his operational career. He joined in the late 1990s as the only officer in the entire CIA fluent in both Greek and Arabic, served as chief of counterintelligence in the bin Laden unit, watched the Center swell from a few hundred employees to nearly 2,000 by September 12, 2001, and it was to CTC that he walked back down in May 2002 to refuse the torture program — the moment, he says, the CIA began to turn on him.

taliban-embassy-raid.title: CIA–FBI interagency rivalry and 9/11
taliban-embassy-raid.summary: John Kiriakou's account of the historical CIA–FBI rivalry, dating to J. Edgar Hoover's opposition to the 1947 National Security Act, and how it manifested before September 11 when Cofer Black's Counterterrorism Center withheld from the FBI that hijackers Nawaf al-Hazmi and Khalid al-Mihdhar had been granted U.S. visas.

taliban-embassy-raid.title: George H.W. Bush
taliban-embassy-raid.summary: The 41st president — and the one John Kiriakou briefed a number of times, finding him "far more worldly" than the others, as befits a former CIA director. Kiriakou credits him with throwing away his presidency by keeping his word and stopping short of Baghdad, faults the ceasefire's helicopter loophole that let Saddam slaughter the Shia, calls him the last president to give the Arabs a fair shake — cutting off loan guarantees until Israel stopped building settlements — and traces the second Iraq war's personal edge to Saddam's 1993 attempt to assassinate him.

taliban-embassy-raid.title: World Trade Center
taliban-embassy-raid.summary: The twin towers whose burning image reached John Kiriakou on the little TV of Cofer Black's secretary — he compared it aloud to the 1930s Empire State Building accident, protested that the day was too clear not to see the tower, and watched the second plane hit as the words left his mouth. Kiriakou ties the towers' story back to the neglected files of the 1990 Kahane assassination and the 1993 bombing, whose captured plotters said they had meant to kill 200,000 by collapsing the buildings into each other — and to John O'Neill, the al-Qaeda-obsessed FBI man who became WTC security chief and died there on his first days at work.

taliban-embassy-raid.title: Tommy McHale
taliban-embassy-raid.summary: Highly decorated Port Authority of New York and New Jersey detective who worked as a terrorist hunter alongside John Kiriakou in Islamabad, Pakistan after 9/11; a survivor of the 1993 World Trade Center bombing whose best friend died on 9/11.

taliban-spokesman-setup.title: FBI
taliban-spokesman-setup.summary: Kiriakou says FBI agents were sticklers for the law in a way the CIA never was — and that the bureau 'leaks like a sieve.'

taliban-spokesman-setup.title: FCI Loretto
taliban-spokesman-setup.summary: U.S. Federal Correctional Institution in Loretto, Pennsylvania; the low-medium-security prison at which John Kiriakou served 23 months of a 30-month sentence following his 2013 Espionage Act–era plea deal; the originally ordered "minimum security work camp" placement was countermanded — per Kiriakou, on Brennan's direct intervention — to place him in the actual prison alongside the general population.

taliban-spokesman-setup.title: Bureau of Prisons
taliban-spokesman-setup.summary: The federal agency that ran John Kiriakou's incarceration — and one of his most persistent post-prison targets. The BOP overrode his judge's camp recommendation by deeming him "a threat to the public safety," threatened him with "diesel therapy" until 1,600 logged phone calls and letters from a dozen House members and two senators backed it off, and, per Kiriakou, functions as "an employment agency for unemployable semi-literate rural white men" and "a dumping ground for failed medical professionals" — an agency for which a prisoner's death is cheaper than his treatment.

taliban-spokesman-setup.title: Central Intelligence Agency
taliban-spokesman-setup.summary: U.S. foreign intelligence service; John Kiriakou's employer from 1990 to 2004 and the central institution of KiriPedia

taliban-spokesman-setup.title: Letter from Loretto
taliban-spokesman-setup.summary: Prison newsletter written by John Kiriakou from FCI Loretto, modeled on Martin Luther King's "Letter from Birmingham Jail," which exposed two crimes committed against him by guards and went viral after being relayed to the Huffington Post, drawing national press to the prison.

taliban-spokesman-setup.title: Administrative remedy process
taliban-spokesman-setup.summary: The Bureau of Prisons' internal grievance system, which Kiriakou describes as a fig leaf designed to run out the clock on prisoners' complaints rather than resolve them.

targeting-analyst.title: Kiriakou's transfer to the Directorate of Operations
targeting-analyst.summary: John Kiriakou's roughly two-month internal campaign to transfer from the CIA's analytic Directorate of Intelligence to the operational Directorate of Operations, overcoming what he calls a "natural bias in operations against the eggheads on the analytic side," followed by an Athens posting secured because he was the only person in the entire CIA fluent in both Greek and Arabic. Covers his full CIA career arc from 1988/1990 recruitment through analyst years on Iraq, the switch to operations, 9/11, the enhanced-interrogation refusal, executive assistant to the deputy director for operations, and his eventual resignation and post-CIA career.

targeting-analyst.title: Enhanced interrogation techniques
targeting-analyst.summary: The CIA's post-9/11 interrogation program; described by John Kiriakou as torture and as a euphemism designed to insulate the responsible officials from legal exposure.

targeting-analyst.title: Abu Zubaydah
targeting-analyst.summary: Detainee captured by John Kiriakou's CIA team in Pakistan in March 2002; the first subject of the agency's enhanced interrogation techniques program; subjected to both approved and unauthorized techniques including the cockroach-in-coffin treatment exploiting a documented insect phobia.

targeting-analyst.title: Magic box
targeting-analyst.summary: An improvised cell-phone locator that two CIA Directorate of Science and Technology officers built from parts bought in a Pakistani bazaar during the hunt for Abu Zubaydah; it could point toward a phone when switched on, but too slowly to act on.

targeting-analyst.title: CIA cash room
targeting-analyst.summary: John Kiriakou's description of the rooms at large CIA stations stacked floor-to-ceiling with cash — tens or hundreds of millions of dollars — from which an officer can sign out whatever an operation needs, as when he took $2 million to buy safe houses for the Abu Zubaydah capture.

targeting-analyst.title: CIA Torture Program Whistleblowing
targeting-analyst.summary: In December 2007, John Kiriakou became the first former CIA officer to publicly confirm the agency's post-9/11 torture program, telling ABC's Brian Ross that torture — including waterboarding — was official U.S. government policy personally approved by the president.
